Chapter 3. Kubernetes and GPUsKubernetes 与 GPU

At its core, generative AI involves intensive mathematical computations, particularly linear algebra operations such as tensor multiplications. These operations demand significant computational power and memory capacity to process large datasets and models ranging from tens to hundreds of billions of parameters. Fortunately, specialized hardware known as Graphics Processing Units (GPUs) has emerged to optimize and accelerate these computational workloads.

生成式 AI 的核心是密集的数学计算，尤其是张量乘法等线性代数运算。这些运算需要巨大的算力与内存，才能处理动辄数百亿参数的数据集与模型。幸运的是，一种被称为图形处理器（GPU）的专用硬件应运而生，用于优化与加速这类计算负载。

Initially designed for rendering graphics and creating immersive gaming experiences, GPUs quickly found their place in the AI domain due to their massively parallel architecture. This capability perfectly aligns with the requirements of linear algebra-heavy tasks involved in AI and machine learning.

GPU 最初为渲染图形、营造沉浸式游戏体验而设计，但凭借其大规模并行架构，它很快在 AI 领域找到了用武之地。这种能力与 AI、机器学习中那些线性代数密集型任务的需求完美契合。

Today, GPUs are the most prevalent type of accelerator in the AI landscape, with NVIDIA leading the market by a large margin, followed by AMD and Intel as its primary competitors. While GPUs dominate, alternative technologies exist, each with unique strengths and ideal use cases. Google’s Tensor Processing Units, for example, offer compelling performance but are typically restricted to the Google ecosystem. Additionally, specialized AI-specific Application-Specific Integrated Circuits (ASICs), such as those developed by Cerebras and Graphcore, as well as Field Programmable Gate Arrays (FPGAs), represent emerging but still niche alternatives.

今天，GPU 是 AI 领域最主流的加速器类型，NVIDIA 大幅领先，AMD 与 Intel 紧随其后。在 GPU 之外也存在其他技术，各有独特优势与理想用例。例如 Google 的张量处理单元（TPU）性能强劲，但通常局限于 Google 生态。此外，Cerebras、Graphcore 开发的专用 AI 专用集成电路（ASIC），以及现场可编程门阵列（FPGA），都是新兴但仍属小众的替代方案。

The primary reason GPUs remain the standard choice is their mature ecosystem, broad availability, and proven scalability. When it comes to deploying LLMs in production, GPUs have become indispensable due to the substantial memory and computational demands these models impose.

GPU 之所以仍是标准选择，主要因为其成熟的生态、广泛的可得性与经过验证的可扩展性。在生产环境部署 LLM 时，由于这些模型对显存与算力的巨大需求，GPU 已变得不可或缺。

By default, Kubernetes includes built-in support for standard computing resources like CPU and memory. However, leveraging specialized hardware, such as GPUs, requires additional mechanisms. Kubernetes addresses this through device plug-ins,

Kubernetes 默认内建对 CPU、内存等标准计算资源的支持。但要利用 GPU 这类专用硬件，就需要额外机制。Kubernetes 通过设备插件（device plug-in）来解决这一问题——

原书第 119 页

a pluggable extension framework. The device plug-ins interface allows Kubernetes to integrate external hardware resources and manage their lifecycle, effectively expanding the Kubernetes API to include these specialized devices.

这是一个可插拔的扩展框架。设备插件接口让 Kubernetes 能够集成外部硬件资源并管理其生命周期，从而有效地把 Kubernetes API 扩展到这些专用设备。

GPUs, however, demand particular attention. They require specific discovery mechanisms and scheduling criteria within Kubernetes, as well as dedicated software stacks, such as NVIDIA’s CUDA libraries, to function correctly.

然而 GPU 需要特别关注。它们在 Kubernetes 中需要专门的发现机制与调度标准，还需要 NVIDIA CUDA 库等专用软件栈才能正确工作。

In this chapter, we will explore Kubernetes’ device integration mechanisms for efficient GPU access and management, specifically targeting NVIDIA GPUs due to their dominance in this space.

本章探讨 Kubernetes 用于高效访问与管理 GPU 的设备集成机制；鉴于 NVIDIA GPU 在该领域的主导地位，我们以它为重点。

We’ll begin by examining how Kubernetes discovers GPU resources using Node Feature Discovery and NVIDIA’s specialized GPU Feature Discovery. Next, we’ll cover the foundational Kubernetes device plug-in mechanism, along with an overview of the emerging Dynamic Resource Allocation (DRA) feature for more flexible GPU allocation.

我们先看 Kubernetes 如何通过 Node Feature Discovery 与 NVIDIA 专用的 GPU Feature Discovery 发现 GPU 资源；接着介绍基础的 Kubernetes 设备插件机制，并概览新兴的 Dynamic Resource Allocation（DRA）特性，它用于更灵活的 GPU 分配。

Scheduling GPU workloads involves careful consideration to ensure efficient utilization of resources. We’ll discuss resource-based GPU scheduling alongside label-based scheduling strategies before exploring advanced GPU management with the NVIDIA GPU Operator. This includes sophisticated GPU partitioning mechanisms like time slicing and Multi-Instance GPU (MIG), plus comprehensive GPU monitoring solutions like the Data Center GPU Manager (DCGM) exporter.

调度 GPU 负载需要仔细考量，以确保资源高效利用。我们会讨论基于资源的 GPU 调度与基于标签的调度策略，然后探讨用 NVIDIA GPU Operator 做高级 GPU 管理——包括时间切片、Multi-Instance GPU（MIG）等精细 GPU 分区机制，以及 Data Center GPU Manager（DCGM）exporter 等全面的 GPU 监控方案。

The chapter also covers multi-GPU inference, focusing on scenarios where a single GPU is insufficient. Here, we’ll describe various techniques like tensor parallelism and pipeline parallelism to leverage multiple GPUs effectively on single or multiple nodes. Finally, we’ll consolidate best practices and optimization strategies to help you manage GPU resources efficiently, prevent fragmentation, and maximize the performance of your Kubernetes cluster.

本章还涵盖多 GPU 推理，聚焦单块 GPU 不够用的场景。我们会描述张量并行、流水线并行等技术，以便在单节点或多节点上高效利用多块 GPU。最后，我们汇总最佳实践与优化策略，帮你高效管理 GPU 资源、防止碎片化、最大化 Kubernetes 集群的性能。

Let’s start by exploring how Kubernetes identifies and labels GPU resources, laying the groundwork for effective GPU management.

我们先从 Kubernetes 如何识别并标注 GPU 资源开始，为有效的 GPU 管理打下基础。

GPU Discovery
GPU 发现

Before Kubernetes can effectively manage GPUs, it must first reliably identify which nodes possess GPUs and determine their capabilities. Accurate hardware detection ensures that workloads match nodes offering suitable GPU resources.

在 Kubernetes 能有效管理 GPU 之前，它必须先可靠地识别哪些节点拥有 GPU、并弄清其能力。准确的硬件检测能确保负载被调度到提供合适 GPU 资源的节点上。

Kubernetes provides a general-purpose solution called Node Feature Discovery, which detects hardware features and applies corresponding labels to nodes. Let’s first take a closer look at how Node Feature Discovery works, followed by NVIDIA’s GPU Feature Discovery.

我们先细看 Node Feature Discovery 的工作原理，再看 NVIDIA 的 GPU Feature Discovery。

Node Feature Discovery

Kubernetes clusters rarely consist of identical nodes. Instead, they’re typically diverse in hardware capabilities—especially when specialized hardware like GPUs are involved. Effective scheduling in such heterogeneous environments—be it cloud deployments, hybrid setups, or bare-metal clusters—depends heavily on accurately identifying these hardware capabilities.

Kubernetes 集群很少由完全相同的节点组成；相反，它们在硬件能力上通常是多样的——尤其在涉及 GPU 这类专用硬件时。在这类异构环境中——无论云部署、混合部署还是裸金属集群——有效调度在很大程度上依赖于准确识别这些硬件能力。

As mentioned previously, the Node Feature Discovery (NFD) project provides this capability. NFD detects hardware features on each node and automatically labels the corresponding node resources in the cluster. These labels provide essential information for the Kubernetes scheduler, enabling intelligent placement of workloads based on available hardware.

如前所述，Node Feature Discovery（NFD）项目提供了这一能力。NFD 检测每个节点上的硬件特性，并自动给集群中相应的节点资源打标签。这些标签为 Kubernetes 调度器提供关键信息，使其能根据可用硬件智能地放置负载。

NFD operates by deploying a DaemonSet across the cluster, ensuring an agent runs on every node. This agent examines the hardware and software configuration of each node, identifying attributes such as CPU details, network interfaces, and available PCI devices like GPUs. Once identified, NFD applies descriptive labels to the node resources in the Kubernetes API.

NFD 通过在集群内部署一个 DaemonSet 来运作，确保每个节点上都运行一个 agent。该 agent 检查每个节点的硬件与软件配置，识别 CPU 详情、网络接口、GPU 等可用 PCI 设备等属性。识别之后，NFD 在 Kubernetes API 中给节点资源打上描述性标签。

Let’s see how you can deploy NFD. You have several options, with the simplest being deployment via Kustomize or Helm, as seen in Example 3-1.

我们看看如何部署 NFD。你有几种选择，最简单的是通过 Kustomize 或 Helm 部署，如例 3-1 所示。

Example 3-1. Installing NFD with Kustomize

NFD_REPO=https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/node-feature-discovery
kubectl apply -k $NFD_REPO/deployment/overlays/default

Alternatively, the NFD operator offers a more integrated management experience, leveraging Kubernetes operators to streamline lifecycle management, especially valuable in production environments.

另一种选择是 NFD operator，它借助 Kubernetes operator 提供更一体化的管理体验，简化生命周期管理，在生产环境中尤其有价值。

Once running, NFD labels nodes automatically. To inspect these labels, you can use a command shown in Example 3-2.

NFD 一旦运行就会自动给节点打标签。要查看这些标签，可以使用例 3-2 所示的命令。

Example 3-2. Inspecting node labels added by NFD

kubectl get node <node-name> -o yaml | yq .metadata.labels

feature.node.kubernetes.io/pci-0300_1d0f.present: "true"
feature.node.kubernetes.io/pci-0302_10de.present: "true"
feature.node.kubernetes.io/cpu-hardware_multithreading: "true"
feature.node.kubernetes.io/cpu-model.family: "6"
feature.node.kubernetes.io/cpu-model.id: "85"
feature.node.kubernetes.io/cpu-model.vendor_id: Intel
feature.node.kubernetes.io/kernel-selinux.enabled: "true"
feature.node.kubernetes.io/kernel-version.full: 5.14.0-427.62.1.el9_4.x86_64
...

  • PCI ID that indicates an AWS (vendor ID 1d0f, device class 0300) VGA compatible display controller, typical in AWS EC2 nodes.PCI ID，表明是一块 AWS（厂商 ID 1d0f，设备类 0300）VGA 兼容显示控制器，常见于 AWS EC2 节点。
  • Indicates the presence of an NVIDIA GPU (vendor ID 10de, device class 0302).表明存在一块 NVIDIA GPU（厂商 ID 10de，设备类 0302）。

NFD labels follow a naming convention starting with feature.node.kubernetes.io/, then specifying hardware category and feature details. By default, NFD follows the format <class>_<vendor> in these labels. The PCI class indicates the general type of device, and the vendor is identified by a standardized PCI vendor ID. The PCI class code 0302 denotes 3D controllers such as GPUs, while vendor IDs include 10de for NVIDIA, 1002 for AMD, and 8086 for Intel. You can customize this labeling in the NFD configuration if you need additional details, such as device or subsystem IDs, for more fine-grained selection.

NFD 标签遵循一种命名约定：以 feature.node.kubernetes.io/ 开头，后跟硬件类别与特性细节。默认情况下，NFD 在这些标签中采用 <class>_<vendor> 的格式。PCI class 表明设备的一般类型，vendor 则由标准化的 PCI 厂商 ID 识别。PCI class code 0302 表示 GPU 等 3D 控制器；厂商 ID 中 10de 为 NVIDIA、1002 为 AMD、8086 为 Intel。如果你需要设备或子系统 ID 等更多细节来做更细粒度的选择，可以在 NFD 配置中自定义这种标签。

However, NFD labels primarily indicate the existence of certain hardware devices rather than detailed GPU specifications, like the GPU model, memory size, or CUDA capabilities. For deeper GPU-specific insights, NVIDIA provides a specialized tool called GPU Feature Discovery, which we explore next.

不过，NFD 标签主要表明某些硬件设备的存在，而非 GPU 型号、显存大小、CUDA 能力等详细规格。要获得更深入的 GPU 专属信息，NVIDIA 提供了一个专用工具 GPU Feature Discovery，下面我们就来探讨。

GPU Feature Discovery

While NFD provides basic hardware labeling capabilities, NVIDIA offers a specialized solution for more detailed GPU information: GPU Feature Discovery (GFD). As part of the NVIDIA GPU Operator, which we’ll discuss in “NVIDIA GPU Operator” on page 95, GFD is a lightweight utility specifically designed to detect detailed GPU characteristics and expose them as node labels for advanced scheduling.

NFD 提供基础的硬件打标能力，而 NVIDIA 为更详细的 GPU 信息提供了专用方案：GPU Feature Discovery（GFD）。作为 NVIDIA GPU Operator 的一部分（我们将在第 95 页“NVIDIA GPU Operator”中讨论），GFD 是一个轻量工具，专门用于检测详细的 GPU 特性并把它们暴露为节点标签，以供高级调度使用。

Similar to NFD, GFD runs as a DaemonSet on GPU-equipped nodes. It inspects the GPUs on each node, utilizing utilities such as nvidia-smi, to gather detailed information like GPU model, memory capacity, CUDA version, and Multi-Instance GPU capabilities. GFD then applies this detailed GPU-specific data as Kubernetes node labels.

与 NFD 类似，GFD 以 DaemonSet 形式运行在配备 GPU 的节点上。它利用 nvidia-smi 等工具检查每个节点上的 GPU，收集 GPU 型号、显存容量、CUDA 版本、Multi-Instance GPU 能力等详细信息，然后把这些 GPU 专属数据作为 Kubernetes 节点标签应用。

Table 3-1 lists several key labels added by GFD, along with their descriptions and examples.

表 3-1 列出了 GFD 添加的几个关键标签，及其说明与示例。

The detailed labels provided by GFD enable advanced scheduling decisions beyond what’s possible with basic NFD labels. For instance, you might use a node selector like nvidia.com/gpu.product: A100-SXM4-40GB-SHARED to target GPUs explicitly configured for time-sharing mode (see “Time slicing” on page 98). Conversely, you can ensure exclusive GPU access by explicitly avoiding nodes with the -SHARED suffix.

GFD 提供的详细标签支持超出基础 NFD 标签能力的高级调度决策。例如，你可以用 nvidia.com/gpu.product: A100-SXM4-40GB-SHARED 这样的节点选择器，专门挑出配置为时间共享模式的 GPU（见第 98 页“时间切片”）；反过来，你也可以显式避开带 -SHARED 后缀的节点，以确保独占 GPU。

In practice, these detailed labels are often used internally by components of the NVIDIA GPU Operator, such as the NVIDIA device plug-in. Typically, users simply request GPU resources directly via resource requests in their pod specifications, as described in “Resource-Based Scheduling” on page 91. Nevertheless, understanding these labels provides valuable insights into Kubernetes’ GPU scheduling mechanisms, especially in complex GPU deployments.

实践中，这些详细标签常被 NVIDIA GPU Operator 的各组件（如 NVIDIA device plug-in）内部使用。通常用户只是在 pod 规范中通过资源请求直接申请 GPU 资源，如第 91 页“基于资源的调度”所述。尽管如此，理解这些标签能让你深入了解 Kubernetes 的 GPU 调度机制，尤其是在复杂 GPU 部署中。

Next, let’s look at how GPUs are enabled and advertised in Kubernetes, starting with the Kubernetes device plug-in framework.

接下来我们看 GPU 如何在 Kubernetes 中被启用并公布，先从 Kubernetes 设备插件框架开始。

Kubernetes GPU Device Plug-Ins
Kubernetes GPU 设备插件

Once you’ve clearly identified and labeled GPU capabilities, the next step is to expose GPUs as schedulable and allocatable resources within Kubernetes. Kubernetes achieves this through its device plug-in framework, which allows external hardware to integrate seamlessly into the Kubernetes resource model.

一旦清晰识别并标注了 GPU 能力，下一步就是把 GPU 暴露为 Kubernetes 内可调度、可分配的资源。Kubernetes 通过其设备插件框架实现这一点，该框架让外部硬件能无缝集成进 Kubernetes 资源模型。

Kubernetes was designed from the ground up to be extensible. While CPUs and memory are natively supported, Kubernetes provides a standardized and extensible framework called device plug-ins for integrating specialized hardware resources such as GPUs, TPUs, and other accelerators.

Kubernetes 从一开始就被设计为可扩展的。CPU 与内存是原生支持的，而 Kubernetes 提供了一个名为设备插件的标准化、可扩展框架，用于集成 GPU、TPU 及其他加速器等专用硬件资源。

These plug-ins register with the Kubelet on each node and advertise device availability and health status directly to Kubernetes, enabling resource-aware scheduling and workload isolation.

这些插件在每个节点上向 Kubelet 注册，并直接向 Kubernetes 公布设备的可用性与健康状态，从而实现资源感知的调度与负载隔离。

The device plug-in interface supports a wide variety of specialized hardware, including FPGAs, networking accelerators, storage controllers, cryptographic modules, multimedia processors, and robotics hardware. Importantly for generative AI, it also supports GPUs and other AI accelerators.

设备插件接口支持种类繁多的专用硬件，包括 FPGA、网络加速器、存储控制器、加密模块、多媒体处理器、机器人硬件。对生成式 AI 而言重要的是，它也支持 GPU 与其他 AI 加速器。

The device plug-in mechanism operates through four core functions:

设备插件机制通过四项核心职能运作：

  • Device discovery. Plug-ins detect hardware devices on nodes and report their inventory to the Kubelet.设备发现。插件检测节点上的硬件设备，并把清单上报给 Kubelet。
  • Resource allocation. When a workload requires specific hardware resources (e.g., GPUs), the device plug-in handles exclusive allocation. It sets up the runtime environment, exposes necessary device files, and injects environment variables.资源分配。当负载需要特定硬件资源（如 GPU）时，设备插件负责独占分配。它搭建运行时环境、暴露必要的设备文件、并注入环境变量。
  • Health monitoring. Plug-ins continuously monitor device health, ensuring Kubernetes is aware of unhealthy hardware to inform scheduling decisions.健康监控。插件持续监控设备健康状况，确保 Kubernetes 知晓不健康的硬件，从而影响调度决策。
  • Scheduler integration. Device plug-ins expose hardware as standard Kubernetes extended resources (e.g., nvidia.com/gpu). Pods request these resources explicitly in their resource declarations, ensuring accurate scheduling to nodes with available devices. For more about resource-based scheduling, see “Resource-Based Scheduling” on page 91.调度器集成。设备插件把硬件暴露为标准的 Kubernetes 扩展资源（如 nvidia.com/gpu）。pod 在资源声明中显式请求这些资源，从而确保被准确调度到有可用设备的节点。关于基于资源的调度，见第 91 页“基于资源的调度”。

    Several well-known device plug-ins provide Kubernetes support for specific vendor hardware. Each of these plug-ins provides Kubernetes integration for the respective vendor’s accelerators and enables workloads to consume GPU or TPU resources as first-class citizens within a Kubernetes cluster:

    有几个知名的设备插件为特定厂商硬件提供 Kubernetes 支持。每个插件都为相应厂商的加速器提供 Kubernetes 集成，让负载能在 Kubernetes 集群内把 GPU 或 TPU 资源当作一等公民来消费：

  • nvidia-device-plugin. Official NVIDIA plug-in exposing CUDA-enabled GPUs in Kubernetes, essential for GPU-accelerated AI workloads. We’ll explore the NVIDIA device plug-in further in the context of the NVIDIA GPU Operator in “NVIDIA GPU Operator” on page 95.nvidia-device-plugin。NVIDIA 官方插件，在 Kubernetes 中暴露支持 CUDA 的 GPU，对 GPU 加速的 AI 负载必不可少。我们将在第 95 页“NVIDIA GPU Operator”中结合 GPU Operator 进一步探讨 NVIDIA device plug-in。
  • amd-device-plugin. Official AMD plug-in integrating ROCm-based GPUs, suitable for high-performance computing and AI workloads.amd-device-plugin。AMD 官方插件，集成基于 ROCm 的 GPU，适合高性能计算与 AI 负载。
  • intel-gpu-plugin. Intel’s plug-in for integrated and discrete GPUs, enabling GPU resources in Kubernetes environments.intel-gpu-plugin。Intel 用于核显与独显的插件，在 Kubernetes 环境中启用 GPU 资源。
  • google-cloud-tpu-device-plugin. Google’s plug-in for integrating Tensor Processing Units (TPUs), specialized hardware optimized for machine learning workloads, exclusively available in the Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE).google-cloud-tpu-device-plugin。Google 用于集成张量处理单元（TPU）的插件；TPU 是为机器学习负载优化的专用硬件，仅在 Google Kubernetes Engine（GKE）中可用。

    • Device plug-ins have become a foundational building block for GPU integration into Kubernetes. However, this approach has limitations. Device plug-ins usually allocate devices exclusively to individual pods, which often leads to underutilized resources. Additionally, resource allocation is static and determined at scheduling time, making it less flexible for workloads with dynamic resource requirements.

    设备插件已成为把 GPU 集成进 Kubernetes 的基础构建块。但这种方式有局限：设备插件通常把设备独占分配给单个 pod，常导致资源利用不足；此外资源分配是静态的、在调度时确定，对资源需求动态变化的负载不够灵活。

    To address these challenges, Kubernetes is evolving toward Dynamic Resource Allocation, which we discuss in “Dynamic Resource Allocation” on page 92. In the meantime, most production environments will continue to rely on the established resource request model for GPU scheduling.

    为应对这些挑战，Kubernetes 正朝着 Dynamic Resource Allocation 演进，我们将在第 92 页“动态资源分配”中讨论。与此同时，大多数生产环境仍会继续沿用成熟的资源请求模型来做 GPU 调度。

    Let’s now take a closer look at how Kubernetes leverages both resource-based and label-based techniques to select the placement of GPU workloads in Kubernetes.

    现在我们细看 Kubernetes 如何结合基于资源与基于标签的技术，来选择 GPU 负载的放置位置。

    GPU Workload Scheduling
    GPU 负载调度

    Kubernetes offers three complementary approaches to placing GPU-bound workloads. The first steers pods with node labels and affinity rules, while the second relies solely on numeric resource requests. The third mechanism that influences automated placement for GPU workloads is based on Dynamic Resource Allocation (DRA). We look at them separately so that the strengths of each method remain clear.

    Kubernetes 提供三种互补的方式来放置 GPU 密集型负载。第一种用节点标签与亲和性规则引导 pod；第二种仅依赖数值化的资源请求；第三种影响 GPU 负载自动放置的机制基于 Dynamic Resource Allocation（DRA）。我们分别考察，以便看清每种方式的长处。

    原书第 125 页

    Let’s begin by examining label-based scheduling, which offers fine-grained control over GPU workload placement.

    我们先看基于标签的调度，它对 GPU 负载的放置提供细粒度控制。

    Label-Based Scheduling
    基于标签的调度

    When a cluster contains several different kinds of GPUs, or when operators want to fence off GPU nodes from general workloads, labels become the steering wheel. Kubernetes offers three closely related mechanisms, each adding a different degree of control: nodeSelector, node affinity, and taints with tolerations.

    当集群中存在多种 GPU、或运维人员想把 GPU 节点与一般负载隔离开时，标签就成了方向盘。Kubernetes 提供三种紧密相关的机制，各提供不同程度的控制力：nodeSelector、node affinity，以及 taints 加 tolerations。

    nodeSelector

    nodeSelector is the most direct approach. You attach a fixed label to every node that matches a certain characteristic, then repeat that exact key-value pair in the pod spec’s nodeSelector field. Instead of creating custom labels manually, you can leverage the GPU-specific labels that the NFD and GFD operators automatically attach to nodes. See “GPU Discovery” on page 82 for details and the GPU-related labels that are available for selection.

    nodeSelector 是最直接的方式。你给每个符合某特征的节点打上一个固定标签，然后在 pod 规范的 nodeSelector 字段中重复同一个键值对。你不必手动创建自定义标签，而可以利用 NFD、GFD operator 自动附加到节点上的 GPU 专属标签。可用的 GPU 相关标签详见第 82 页“GPU 发现”。

    As seen in Example 3-3, the beauty of nodeSelector is its simplicity. A single line pins the workload to the desired node pool, with no extra scheduler overhead. However, the rule is absolute: if the label is missing or misspelled, the pod won’t schedule. nodeSelector also can’t express alternatives; it’s “T4 or nothing.”

    如例 3-3 所示，nodeSelector 的妙处在于简单。一行配置就把负载钉到目标节点池，没有额外调度开销。但规则是绝对的：标签缺失或拼错，pod 就调度不上去。nodeSelector 也无法表达备选项——它是“要么 T4，要么没有”。

    Example 3-3. Direct selection of a node with a node selector

    apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: t4-inference
spec:
  containers:
  - name: server
    image: myrepo/llm-server:latest
  nodeSelector:
    # Select only nodes that are labelled for a Tesla T4 GPU
    nvidia.com/gpu.product: Tesla-T4

    Node affinity

    Node affinity builds on the same idea but allows richer expressions and soft preferences. Required terms act like an extended selector, while preferred terms let you nudge the scheduler toward the best node when several satisfy the hard constraints. Example 3-4 demonstrates this flexibility. This example relies on the labels added by the GFD, as described in “GPU Feature Discovery” on page 84.

    Node affinity 基于同样的思路，但允许更丰富的表达式与软偏好。required 条件像扩展的选择器，preferred 条件则让你在多个节点都满足硬约束时，轻轻推动调度器偏向最佳节点。例 3-4 展示了这种灵活性。该例依赖 GFD 添加的标签，如第 84 页“GPU Feature Discovery”所述。

    原书第 126 页

    Example 3-4. Node affinity for finer-grained selections

    apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: a100-preferred
spec:
  containers:
  - name: llm
    image: myrepo/mt-server:latest
    resources:
      limits:
        nvidia.com/gpu: 4
  affinity:
    nodeAffinity:
      requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
        nodeSelectorTerms:
        - matchExpressions:
          - key: nvidia.com/gpu.memory
            operator: Gt
            values: ["40000"]
      preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
      - weight: 1
        preference:
          matchExpressions:
          - key: nvidia.com/gpu.family
            operator: In
            values: ["hopper"]
    • Required conditions for a node to be considered as a scheduling target. In this example, the GPU needs at least 40 GB memory.节点被视为调度目标所需满足的硬条件。本例要求 GPU 至少有 40 GB 显存。
    • NVIDIA H100 is preferred, but it will be OK if no H100 is available.优先选 NVIDIA H100，但没有 H100 也可以接受。

    With affinity, you insist on a minimum memory size, then express a gentle preference for Hopper (H100) over Ampere (A100). If no Hopper node is free, Kubernetes schedules the pod on an Ampere node that meets the memory requirement. The downside is verbosity: long match expressions can clutter manifests, and too many hard clauses can starve the workload.

    用 affinity，你坚持最小显存要求，然后表达对 Hopper（H100）略偏好于 Ampere（A100）。如果没有空闲的 Hopper 节点，Kubernetes 就把 pod 调度到满足显存要求的 Ampere 节点。缺点是冗长：长长的 match 表达式会让 manifest 杂乱，硬条款太多还可能让负载无节点可调度。

    Taints and tolerations

    Sometimes operators want to flip the model and mark certain nodes as off-limits unless a pod explicitly opts in. A taint added by the administrator repels all pods; only those carrying a matching toleration can schedule.

    有时运维人员想反过来：把某些节点标记为禁止入内，除非 pod 显式选择加入。管理员加的 taint 会排斥所有 pod；只有携带匹配 toleration 的 pod 才能被调度上去。

    In Example 3-5, we add a taint key-value pair nvidia.com/gpu=true with the taint effect NoSchedule to all nodes carrying the label nvidia.com/gpu.count. Only pods that explicitly tolerate the nvidia.com/gpu constraint can be scheduled on these nodes.

    在例 3-5 中，我们给所有带 nvidia.com/gpu.count 标签的节点加上一个 taint 键值对 nvidia.com/gpu=true，效果为 NoSchedule。只有显式容忍 nvidia.com/gpu 这一约束的 pod 才能被调度到这些节点上。

    原书第 127 页

    Example 3-5. Taint a node to be not considered for scheduling by default

    # cluster-admin permission required
kubectl taint nodes -l nvidia.com/gpu.count nvidia.com/gpu=true:NoSchedule

    Such a toleration is shown in Example 3-6, which allows it to be scheduled on nodes with a taint nvidia.com/gpu, regardless of the value.

    例 3-6 展示了这样一个 toleration，它允许 pod 被调度到带 nvidia.com/gpu taint 的节点上，无论值是什么。

    Example 3-6. Deployment with a toleration for nvidia.com/gpu taints

    apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: gpu-serving
spec:
  replicas: 2
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: tgi
        image: ghcr.io/huggingface/tgi:latest
        resources:
          limits:
            nvidia.com/gpu: 1
      tolerations:
      - key: "nvidia.com/gpu"
        operator: "Exists"
        effect: "NoSchedule"
    • Require an nvidia.com/gpu resource as set by the NVIDIA device plug-in. We explain resource-based scheduling in “Resource-Based Scheduling” on page 91.申请一个由 NVIDIA device plug-in 设置的 nvidia.com/gpu 资源。基于资源的调度见第 91 页“基于资源的调度”。
    • Tolerations that ignore nvidia.com/gpu taints regardless of value, so that this deployment can also be deployed on those nodes.无论值为何都容忍 nvidia.com/gpu taint，以便该 deployment 也能部署到这些节点。

    Taints are ideal for dedicating costly GPU nodes to GPU workloads or for cordoning nodes under maintenance. They work well in tandem with affinity or selectors: the taint keeps general pods out, while affinity decides which GPU node is the best fit among those that remain.

    Taint 非常适合把昂贵的 GPU 节点专用于 GPU 负载，或在维护时隔离节点。它与 affinity 或选择器配合得很好：taint 把一般 pod 挡在外面，affinity 则在剩下的 GPU 节点中决定哪个最合适。

    More details about the various ways to influence Kubernetes’ scheduling decisions can be found in the Automated Placement pattern in Kubernetes Patterns. But which placement technique should be used in which context? It depends on the following:

    关于影响 Kubernetes 调度决策的各种方式，更多细节见《Kubernetes Patterns》中的 Automated Placement 模式。但到底哪种放置技术该用在什么场景？取决于以下几点：

  • nodeSelector shines in small, homogeneous GPU fleets where a single label is enough.nodeSelector 在小型、同质的 GPU 机队中表现出色——单个标签就够了。
  • Node affinity becomes the tool of choice once you mix generations, memory sizes, or availability zones.一旦混用不同代际、显存大小或可用区，node affinity 就成了首选工具。
    • 原书第 128 页
  • Taints protect the GPU pool at cluster scope and pair naturally with the other two techniques for fine placement.Taint 在集群范围内保护 GPU 池，并与另外两种精细放置技术天然搭配。

    • All three approaches share one limitation: they rely on static labels that administrators either maintain manually or are added by discovery operators like the NFD and GFD that we described in “GPU Discovery” on page 82.

    这三种方式有一个共同局限：它们都依赖静态标签——要么由管理员手动维护，要么由 NFD、GFD 等发现 operator 添加（见第 82 页“GPU 发现”）。

    While these label-based approaches offer fine-grained control, they require knowing and managing specific node labels. For simpler use cases where any available GPU will suffice, there is a more straightforward approach: resource-based scheduling.

    虽然这些基于标签的方式提供细粒度控制，但它们要求你了解并管理特定的节点标签。对于“随便哪块可用 GPU 都行”的更简单用例，有一种更直接的方式：基于资源的调度。

    Resource-Based Scheduling
    基于资源的调度

    The simplest way to schedule a GPU workload in Kubernetes is to declare the need for a GPU directly in the workload specification. As soon as the NVIDIA device plug-in is running on the nodes, it advertises every GPU as an extended resource—typically nvidia.com/gpu. A container that sets a limit as shown in Example 3-7 asks the Kubernetes scheduler to find a node with at least one free GPU.

    在 Kubernetes 中调度 GPU 负载最简单的方式，是在负载规范中直接声明需要一块 GPU。一旦 NVIDIA device plug-in 在节点上运行，它就把每块 GPU 公布为一个扩展资源——通常是 nvidia.com/gpu。一个容器若像例 3-7 那样设置 limit，就是在请 Kubernetes 调度器找一个至少有一块空闲 GPU 的节点。

    Example 3-7. Require one NVIDIA GPU

    resources:
  limits:
    nvidia.com/gpu: 1

    The scheduler examines only the numeric availability from the device plug-in, then binds the pod to a qualifying node. The kubelet grants the container exclusive access to one of that node’s GPUs. There are no extra labels to manage, no node selectors to remember, and no additional controllers to install. The mechanism is completely integrated with the familiar requests and limits resource model, so it feels like asking for CPU or memory—just with a different resource name.

    调度器只看设备插件上报的数值可用性，然后把 pod 绑到一个合格节点。kubelet 把该节点上一块 GPU 独占授予容器。没有额外标签要管理、没有节点选择器要记、没有额外控制器要安装。这一机制完全集成在熟悉的 requests/limits 资源模型里，感觉就像申请 CPU 或内存——只是资源名不同。

    That ease of use is its greatest strength. A single field in the pod spec is enough to isolate the GPU at the device-file level, prevent other pods from touching it, and let CUDA applications run without further configuration. Small clusters with one GPU type, or development environments where any GPU will do, rarely need more than this.

    这种易用性是它最大的长处。pod 规范里一个字段，就足以在设备文件层面隔离 GPU、防止其他 pod 触碰、并让 CUDA 应用无需额外配置即可运行。单一 GPU 类型的小集群，或“随便哪块 GPU 都行”的开发环境，几乎都只需要这么多。

    The downside is the lack of precision. All GPUs appear identical to the scheduler, even if the cluster contains V100s, A100s, or consumer-grade cards. A model that fits comfortably on an 80-GB A100 might not fit on a 16-GB T4, yet a plain nvidia.com/gpu: 1 request treats them the same. There is also no built-in way to request a specific compute capability, restrict pods to GPUs in Multi-Instance GPU mode, or ask for more than one GPU on a node with a particular interconnect topology.

    缺点是不够精确。在调度器看来所有 GPU 都一样——即便集群里有 V100、A100 或消费级显卡。一个在 80 GB A100 上跑得舒服的模型，在 16 GB T4 上可能放不下，但一句普通的 nvidia.com/gpu: 1 请求对它们一视同仁。也没有内建方式来请求特定计算能力、把 pod 限制在 Multi-Instance GPU 模式的 GPU 上，或要求在具有特定互连拓扑的节点上使用多块 GPU。

    原书第 129 页

    In practice, teams work around this limitation by leveraging labels added by the GPU device plug-in (such as nvidia.com/gpu.product) or tagging nodes with custom labels (such as gpu-type=A100), and then combining the resource request with a nodeSelector or nodeAffinity rule to steer workloads to compatible hardware. It’s a powerful tool, but it comes at the cost of extra coordination between the node inventory and the workload definitions.

    实践中，团队会绕开这一限制：利用 GPU 设备插件添加的标签（如 nvidia.com/gpu.product），或给节点打自定义标签（如 gpu-type=A100），再把资源请求与 nodeSelector 或 nodeAffinity 规则结合，把负载引导到兼容硬件上。这是个强大的工具，但代价是节点清单与负载定义之间需要额外协调。

    A more elegant way to express nuanced requirements is the Dynamic Resource Allocation mechanism described in “Dynamic Resource Allocation” on page 92. With DRA, you don’t need to hardcode label conventions or rely on static resource requests. Instead, you declare what kind of GPU you want, and Kubernetes dynamically allocates a matching one.

    表达细微需求的一种更优雅方式，是第 92 页“动态资源分配”中描述的 Dynamic Resource Allocation 机制。用 DRA，你不必硬编码标签约定，也不必依赖静态资源请求；你声明想要哪种 GPU，Kubernetes 就动态分配一块匹配的。

    Dynamic Resource Allocation
    动态资源分配（DRA）

    The Kubernetes device plug-in mechanism made it possible to expose GPUs and other specialized hardware as schedulable resources. With it, workloads request accelerators like nvidia.com/gpu, and Kubernetes allocates them exclusively to a pod at scheduling time. While this works well for many scenarios, it’s a static model. The scheduler cannot distinguish between devices, fixes allocation at scheduling time, and always allocates them exclusively. In practice, this can lead to underutilized resources, coarse-grained scheduling decisions, and limitations when dealing with more advanced GPU configurations like Multi-Instance GPU or time-slicing that we discuss in “Sub-GPU Allocation” on page 98.

    Kubernetes 设备插件机制使 GPU 及其他专用硬件能作为可调度资源暴露出来。借助它，负载申请 nvidia.com/gpu 等加速器，Kubernetes 在调度时把它们独占分配给 pod。虽然这在很多场景下很好用，但它是一个静态模型：调度器无法区分设备、在调度时就固定分配、且总是独占分配。实践中，这会导致资源利用不足、调度决策粗粒度，以及在处理 Multi-Instance GPU、时间切片等更高级 GPU 配置时受限——这些我们将在第 98 页“子 GPU 分配”中讨论。

    DRA is an effort to make device scheduling in Kubernetes more flexible, composable, and dynamic, and it has been available as a core, stable Kubernetes feature since version 1.34. Instead of tying device allocation directly to resource fields in the pod specification, DRA introduces a new set of resource types. These abstractions shift the focus from “how many” devices to “what kind” of device a workload requires. The model is inspired by Kubernetes’ volume provisioning, where users describe a desired resource and let the platform resolve it.

    DRA 旨在让 Kubernetes 中的设备调度更灵活、更可组合、更动态；自 1.34 版本起，它已成为 Kubernetes 的核心稳定特性。DRA 不再把设备分配直接绑定到 pod 规范中的资源字段，而是引入一组新的资源类型。这些抽象把关注点从设备“数量”转向负载所需设备的“种类”。该模型受 Kubernetes 卷供应启发：用户描述想要的资源，由平台去解析。

    With DRA, workloads declare their device needs via ResourceClaimTemplate resources. These templates act as intent declarations. The Kubernetes control plane and the installed DRA driver resolve them at scheduling time. This enables features that are difficult or impossible with static device plug-ins. For instance, a pod can request a specific device class, like an A100 GPU with at least 40 GB (≈ 37 GiB) of memory. The scheduler will place the pod only on a node that can fulfill this

    用 DRA，负载通过 ResourceClaimTemplate 资源声明自己的设备需求。这些模板充当意图声明，由 Kubernetes 控制面与已安装的 DRA 驱动在调度时解析。这带来了静态设备插件难以或无法实现的特性。例如，一个 pod 可以请求特定设备类别，如一块至少 40 GB（约 37 GiB）显存的 A100 GPU。调度器只会把 pod 放到能满足这一

    原书第 130 页

    requirement. The allocation happens just-in-time, allowing for smarter decisions and more efficient usage.

    要求的节点上。分配是即时（just-in-time）进行的，从而能做出更智能的决策、实现更高效的利用。

    This flexibility becomes particularly useful when running LLM inference workloads that require specific GPU types, such as A100s with 80 GB of memory. With DRA, you can request exactly that configuration. This approach doesn’t rely on node labels or manual pod placement.

    当运行需要特定 GPU 类型的 LLM 推理负载（例如 80 GB 显存的 A100）时，这种灵活性尤其有用。用 DRA，你可以精确地请求那种配置，而不必依赖节点标签或手动放置 pod。

    Example 3-8 illustrates this more advanced use case. We define a ResourceClaimTemplate that requests a GPU belonging to the A100 class, with at least 40 GB of memory. We also define the allocation mode and count explicitly. This level of detail is something traditional resource requests cannot express.

    例 3-8 演示了这个更高级的用例。我们定义一个 ResourceClaimTemplate，请求一块属于 A100 类别、显存至少 40 GB 的 GPU；还显式定义了分配模式与数量。这种细节程度是传统资源请求无法表达的。

    Example 3-8. ResourceClaimTemplate defining GPU requirements for deployment pods

    apiVersion: resource.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: ResourceClaimTemplate
metadata:
  name: a100-claim-template
spec:
  spec:
    devices:
      requests:
        - name: high-memory-gpu
          deviceClassName: gpu.nvidia.com/a100
          allocationMode: ExactCount
          count: 1
          parameters:
            minMemory: "40Gi"
            migMode: "disabled"
    • Requests an NVIDIA A100 GPU.请求一块 NVIDIA A100 GPU。
    • One GPU required.需要一块 GPU。
    • GPU needs must have at least 40 Gi of memory, and Multi-Instance GPU mode must be disabled.GPU 至少要有 40 Gi 显存，且必须禁用 Multi-Instance GPU 模式。

    In Example 3-8, we reference a logical device class called gpu.nvidia.com/a100, a level of abstraction that could include A100s with different configurations. We also ask for at least 40 GB of memory and explicitly opt out of Multi-Instance GPU mode to ensure full GPU access.

    在例 3-8 中，我们引用了一个名为 gpu.nvidia.com/a100 的逻辑设备类别——这一层抽象可以涵盖不同配置的 A100。我们还要求至少 40 GB 显存，并显式选择退出 Multi-Instance GPU 模式，以确保独占整块 GPU。

    The workload defined in Example 3-9 then references this template in its resource claims. Kubernetes allocates the actual GPU only at scheduling time, and only if a matching device is available on one of the nodes.

    例 3-9 中定义的负载随后在其 resource claims 中引用这个模板。Kubernetes 只在调度时才分配真实 GPU，且仅当某个节点上有匹配设备可用时才分配。

    原书第 131 页

    Example 3-9. Deployment using ResourceClaimTemplate for GPU allocation

    apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: inference-server
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: model-runner
        image: myorg/llm-inference:latest
        resources:
          claims:
          - name: high-memory-gpu
      resourceClaims:
      - name: high-memory-gpu
        resourceClaimTemplateName: a100-claim-template
    • Reference to a resource claim that should be used when the deployment creates one or more pods.对一个资源 claim 的引用；deployment 创建一个或多个 pod 时应使用它。
    • Reference to the ResourceClaimTemplate defined in Example 3-8.对例 3-8 中定义的 ResourceClaimTemplate 的引用。

    The separation between the declaration and the actual allocation is what makes DRA so powerful. It opens the door for dynamic, demand-driven GPU provisioning—something that’s difficult or impossible with traditional device plug-ins. It also allows drivers to perform more intelligent allocation strategies under the hood. Instead of a simple “pick the first available GPU,” allocation can now consider current usage, power consumption, memory pressure, or other node-level constraints.

    声明与实际分配的分离，正是 DRA 强大之处。它为动态、按需的 GPU 供应打开了大门——这是传统设备插件难以或无法做到的。它还允许驱动在底层执行更智能的分配策略。分配不再是简单的“挑第一块可用 GPU”，而可以考虑当前使用情况、功耗、显存压力或其他节点级约束。

    There are, however, a few caveats. DRA is not yet widely supported in production. As of early 2026, the core DRA APIs are generally available and enabled by default since Kubernetes 1.34, but the ecosystem around it is still catching up. The NVIDIA GPU DRA driver exists, but it is marked as a technical preview and is not yet supported for production environments. Features like partial GPU requests, fine-grained Multi-Instance GPU partitioning, or topology-aware scheduling are still maturing and remain driver- and platform-dependent. Also, integration with cluster autoscalers or quota enforcement is limited.

    不过有几点注意事项。DRA 在生产中尚未被广泛支持。截至 2026 年初，核心 DRA API 已 GA、自 Kubernetes 1.34 起默认启用，但周边生态仍在追赶。NVIDIA GPU DRA 驱动已经存在，但标记为技术预览，尚不支持生产环境。部分 GPU 请求、细粒度 Multi-Instance GPU 分区、拓扑感知调度等特性仍在成熟中，且依赖具体驱动与平台。此外，它与集群自动扩缩器或配额 enforcement 的集成也有限。

    Still, the potential is clear. DRA opens up Kubernetes to more intelligent GPU placement strategies, enables device sharing without resorting to hacks, and brings a more declarative mindset to accelerator provisioning. You no longer need to rely on static node labels, taints, or specialized resource counts to describe what your workload actually needs. Instead, you express the intent, and let Kubernetes and the driver handle the rest.

    尽管如此，其潜力是清晰的。DRA 让 Kubernetes 能采用更智能的 GPU 放置策略，让设备共享不必靠 hack 实现，并为加速器供应带来更声明式的思路。你不再需要依赖静态节点标签、taint 或专门的资源计数来描述负载真正需要什么；你表达意图，剩下的交给 Kubernetes 与驱动。

    原书第 132 页

    As DRA matures, it is likely to become the standard way of handling advanced hardware resources in Kubernetes. We expect vendors like NVIDIA to integrate their device plug-ins, GPU operators, and runtime libraries with DRA to provide a seamless experience for both inference and training workloads.

    随着 DRA 成熟，它很可能成为 Kubernetes 中处理高级硬件资源的标准方式。我们预计 NVIDIA 等厂商会把它们的设备插件、GPU operator 与运行时库与 DRA 集成，为推理与训练负载都提供无缝体验。

    Until DRA becomes production-grade, however, the combination of resource requests and label-based scheduling remains the standard approach for GPU scheduling.

    但在 DRA 达到生产级之前，资源请求与基于标签的调度相结合，仍是 GPU 调度的标准方式。

    NVIDIA GPU Operator

    The previous sections showed how the Kubernetes device plug-in exposes GPUs as schedulable resources (“Kubernetes GPU Device Plug-Ins” on page 86) and how GFD enriches nodes with detailed NVIDIA-specific labels (“GPU Feature Discovery” on page 84). The NVIDIA GPU Operator builds on both pieces and adds everything needed to run NVIDIA GPU workloads reliably in production. It installs drivers, container runtime hooks, and monitoring agents, and it offers two sharing mechanisms for sub-GPU resource allocations in one declarative interface.

    前面几节展示了 Kubernetes 设备插件如何把 GPU 暴露为可调度资源（第 86 页“Kubernetes GPU 设备插件”），以及 GFD 如何用详细的 NVIDIA 专属标签丰富节点（第 84 页“GPU Feature Discovery”）。NVIDIA GPU Operator 在这两者之上构建，并加上了在生产中可靠运行 NVIDIA GPU 负载所需的一切。它安装驱动、容器 runtime hook 与监控 agent，并在一个声明式接口中提供两种子 GPU 资源分配的共享机制。

    The operator automates the installation and configuration of all necessary components, enabling GPU workloads to run efficiently and reliably.

    该 operator 自动化安装与配置所有必要组件，使 GPU 负载能高效、可靠地运行。

    The following components are part of the NVIDIA GPU Operator:

    以下组件属于 NVIDIA GPU Operator：

  • NVIDIA drivers (kernel module and CUDA). At the heart of GPU enablement are the NVIDIA drivers—the kernel modules and user-space libraries that enable CUDA and GPU acceleration. The GPU Operator can deploy the official NVIDIA driver into each GPU node by running a privileged driver container. This container compiles the driver for the node’s kernel or retrieves a precompiled version when available. By containerizing driver installation, the operator ensures all GPU nodes have the required driver version without manual intervention.NVIDIA 驱动（内核模块与 CUDA）。GPU 使能的核心是 NVIDIA 驱动——启用 CUDA 与 GPU 加速的内核模块与用户态库。GPU Operator 可以通过运行一个特权驱动容器，把官方 NVIDIA 驱动部署到每个 GPU 节点。该容器为节点内核编译驱动，或在有预编译版本时直接取用。通过把驱动安装容器化，operator 确保所有 GPU 节点都具备所需驱动版本，而无需人工干预。

    • GPU nodes and OS kernel versions

    GPU nodes ideally should run the same OS kernel version if you want to rely on the operator’s driver container across all nodes. Mixed OS versions might require pre-installing drivers manually. The operator’s ClusterPolicy CR shown in Example 3-11 allows customizing the driver version or using precompiled binaries, if needed.

    如果你想在所有节点上统一依靠 operator 的驱动容器，理想情况下各 GPU 节点应运行相同的 OS 内核版本。混合 OS 版本可能需要手动预安装驱动。例 3-11 所示的 operator ClusterPolicy CR 允许在需要时自定义驱动版本或使用预编译二进制。

  • Kubernetes device plug-in for GPUs. The operator deploys the NVIDIA device plug-in as a DaemonSet on GPU nodes. We already covered the Kubernetes device plug-in architecture in “Kubernetes GPU Device Plug-Ins” on page 86 and how it introduces a new extended resource nvidia.com/gpu that can be used for resource-level scheduling, described in “Resource-Based Scheduling” on page 91. The NVIDIA Kubernetes device plug-ins also allow for sub-GPU allocation, as we will see later in “Sub-GPU Allocation” on page 98. The NVIDIA device plug-in is a critical component; if it’s not running or not working, your pods will be stuck pending because Kubernetes thinks no resources are available.Kubernetes GPU 设备插件。operator 把 NVIDIA 设备插件作为 DaemonSet 部署在 GPU 节点上。我们已在第 86 页“Kubernetes GPU 设备插件”中介绍了设备插件架构，以及它如何引入新的扩展资源 nvidia.com/gpu 用于资源级调度（见第 91 页“基于资源的调度”）。NVIDIA Kubernetes 设备插件还支持子 GPU 分配，我们将在第 98 页“子 GPU 分配”中看到。NVIDIA 设备插件是关键组件：如果它没运行或不正常，pod 会一直 pending，因为 Kubernetes 认为没有可用资源。

The GPU Operator deploys this toolkit on the nodes. The container runtime is essentially an extension to CRI-O and containerd that knows how to inject GPU drivers and device files into containers when a GPU is requested. The operator manages the container runtime automatically, eliminating the need to manually configure NVIDIA support. The result is that any container that requests a GPU will have the necessary /dev/nvidia0 device and GPU drivers available. Without it, an administrator would have to log in remotely to the node and use nvidia-smi to set up MIG partitions manually. The GPU Operator takes care of this, keeping MIG setups declarative.Multi-Instance GPU（MIG）Manager。在具备 MIG 能力 GPU（如 NVIDIA A100 或 H100 卡）的系统上，operator 包含一个 MIG Manager 组件。该服务监控节点的 MIG 配置，并能按期望状态重新配置 GPU 的 MIG 分区。它默认运行在支持 MIG 的节点上，并应用你在 ClusterPolicy 中配置的 MIG 策略——我们将在第 98 页“子 GPU 分配”讨论 GPU 共享选项时展开。MIG Manager 确保：如果某节点应处于 MIG 模式、并切出特定 profile，它会在启动或变更时自动完成。没有它，管理员就得远程登录节点、用 nvidia-smi 手动设置 MIG 分区。GPU Operator 把这些都接管了，让 MIG 设置保持声明式。

DCGM polls every GPU for utilization, memory pressure, ECC errors, temperature, power draw, and a wealth of other counters, translating them into Prometheus metrics. Most users scrape the Exporter with the cluster’s Prometheus stack and surface graphs in Grafana.
