    Operator Configuration with ClusterPolicy
    用 ClusterPolicy 配置 Operator

    The NVIDIA GPU Operator is available for multiple Kubernetes distributions, including OpenShift, where it comes out-of-the-box as part of the OperatorHub catalog. It can also be installed on standard Kubernetes clusters using Helm charts or custom manifests provided by NVIDIA, as shown in Example 3-10.

    NVIDIA GPU Operator 适用于多种 Kubernetes 发行版，包括 OpenShift——后者在 OperatorHub 目录中开箱即带。它也可以用 Helm chart 或 NVIDIA 提供的自定义 manifest 安装到标准 Kubernetes 集群上，如例 3-10 所示。

    Example 3-10. Installing the GPU Operator with Helm

    helm repo add nvidia https://helm.ngc.nvidia.com/nvidia
helm repo update
helm install gpu-operator nvidia/gpu-operator \
  --namespace gpu-operator \
  --create-namespace

    You configure the operator through the ClusterPolicy custom resource. This resource controls all aspects of the GPU operator components, including the device plug-in configuration, enabling time slicing, and configuring MIG strategies. A ClusterPolicy can reference a custom ConfigMap to fine-tune the device plug-in behavior, for example, to enable time slicing or other GPU sharing mechanisms. In the ClusterPolicy, you can specify a key from the ConfigMap that serves as a default if a GPU-enabled node is not labeled with a specific key of nvidia.com/device-plugin.config=<key from configmap>.

    你通过 ClusterPolicy 自定义资源来配置 operator。该资源控制 GPU operator 各组件的方方面面，包括设备插件配置、启用时间切片、配置 MIG 策略。ClusterPolicy 可以引用一个自定义 ConfigMap 来微调设备插件行为，例如启用时间切片或其他 GPU 共享机制。在 ClusterPolicy 中，你可以指定 ConfigMap 中的一个键作为默认值——当某个 GPU 节点没有被打上 nvidia.com/device-plugin.config=<configmap 中的键> 标签时使用。

    Example 3-11 shows a path to a custom ConfigMap for configuring the device plug-in, enables the GPU Feature Discovery, and sets the MIG strategy to mixed.

    例 3-11 展示了：引用一个自定义 ConfigMap 来配置设备插件、启用 GPU Feature Discovery，并把 MIG 策略设为 mixed。

    Example 3-11. Example configuration for the NVIDIA GPU Operator

    apiVersion: nvidia.com/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: gpu-cluster-policy
spec:
  gfd:
    enabled: true
  devicePlugin:
    config:
      name: gpu-sharing-config
      default: sharing
  mig:
    strategy: mixed
    • Enable the GPU Feature Discovery.启用 GPU Feature Discovery。
    • Point to the ConfigMap gpu-sharing-config that has extra configuration information, such as for configuring time slicing.指向 ConfigMap gpu-sharing-config，其中包含额外配置信息，例如用于配置时间切片。
    原书第 135 页
    • The default references a key in the ConfigMap. If set to an empty string, no default applies and nodes must be labeled with nvidia.com/device-plugin.config=<config map key> to pick up the device plug-in config.default 引用 ConfigMap 中的一个键。若设为空字符串，则不应用默认值，节点必须被打上 nvidia.com/device-plugin.config=<config map 键> 标签才能采用设备插件配置。
    • Set the MIG strategy to mixed. See “Multi-Instance GPU” on page 100 for more information about Multi-Instance GPU.把 MIG 策略设为 mixed。关于 Multi-Instance GPU 的更多信息见第 100 页“Multi-Instance GPU”。

    Sub-GPU Allocation
    子 GPU 分配

    The NVIDIA GPU Operator supports advanced GPU features for partitioning or slicing a single GPU among multiple workloads. While sub-GPU resource allocation might not have big relevance for operating LLMs, it’s still important to understand to optimize your GPU usage.

    NVIDIA GPU Operator 支持把单块 GPU 分区或切分给多个负载使用的高级 GPU 特性。虽然子 GPU 资源分配在运维 LLM 时未必那么重要，但理解它对优化 GPU 使用仍很关键。

    The operator supports two modes, which can also be combined:

    operator 支持两种模式，二者也可组合：

  • Time slicing. Allows multiple containers to share a GPU by allocating time-based slices.时间切片。通过按时间分配片，让多个容器共享一块 GPU。
  • MIG. Available on certain GPUs (like A100 and H100) to partition a single GPU into isolated instances.MIG。在特定 GPU（如 A100、H100）上可用，把单块 GPU 分区为相互隔离的实例。

    • One of the powerful capabilities that the NVIDIA GPU Operator enables is sharing a GPU among multiple workloads. This is especially relevant for AI inference or serving multiple models, where you might not always need an entire GPU for each process.

    NVIDIA GPU Operator 所赋能的一项强大能力，就是让一块 GPU 在多个负载间共享。这对 AI 推理或服务多个模型尤其相关——你未必每个进程都需要整块 GPU。

    Let’s demystify these.

    我们来揭开它们的面纱。

    Time slicing
    时间切片

    By default, if a pod requests a GPU (nvidia.com/gpu: 1 in its resource requirements), Kubernetes grants it exclusive access to one physical GPU. Time slicing is a feature that allows oversubscription of GPUs—i.e., advertising more than one virtual GPU per physical GPU, so the scheduler can place multiple pods on the same GPU simultaneously. The NVIDIA device plug-in (when configured accordingly) will create GPU replicas for each real GPU. For example, you could configure one physical GPU to be represented as four devices, allowing up to four pods to each get what they think is one GPU, all actually running on the same hardware. The GPU workloads of these pods will interleave in time on the single GPU. Think of it like CPU time-sharing: if you have a 16-core CPU, you could schedule more than 16 CPU-bound processes by context switching. Each gets a slice of time on the cores, but not all can run at full speed simultaneously. GPU time slicing works the same way.

    默认情况下，如果一个 pod 请求一块 GPU（资源需求中写 nvidia.com/gpu: 1），Kubernetes 就把一块物理 GPU 独占授予它。时间切片是一种允许 GPU 超额订阅的特性——即每块物理 GPU 公布多个虚拟 GPU，让调度器能把多个 pod 同时放到同一块 GPU 上。NVIDIA 设备插件（在相应配置下）会为每块真实 GPU 创建 GPU 副本。例如，你可以把一块物理 GPU 配置为代表 4 个设备，允许最多 4 个 pod 各自拿到一块它们以为的 GPU，而实际上都跑在同一硬件上。这些 pod 的 GPU 负载会在时间上交错使用这块 GPU。把它想象成 CPU 分时：如果你有一块 16 核 CPU，可以通过上下文切换调度超过 16 个 CPU 密集型进程，每个都分到核上的一段时间片，但并非所有进程都能同时全速运行。GPU 时间切片也是这个道理。

    原书第 136 页

    To enable GPU time slicing in your cluster, you configure the device plug-in via a ConfigMap that is referenced in the operator’s configuration, as shown in Example 3-11. The corresponding ConfigMap is shown in Example 3-12.

    要在集群中启用 GPU 时间切片，你通过一个 ConfigMap 配置设备插件——该 ConfigMap 在 operator 配置中被引用，如例 3-11 所示。对应的 ConfigMap 见例 3-12。

    Example 3-12. Example configuration for time slicing

    apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: gpu-sharing-config
  namespace: gpu-operator-resources
data:
  sharing: |
    version: v1
    sharing:
      timeslicing:
        renameByDefault: true
        resources:
        - name: nvidia.com/gpu
          replicas: 8
    • When set to true, renames the resource from nvidia.com/gpu to nvidia.com/gpu.shared. This makes it easier to distinguish shared GPU instances from exclusive ones.设为 true 时，把资源从 nvidia.com/gpu 重命名为 nvidia.com/gpu.shared，便于区分共享 GPU 实例与独占实例。
    • Overcommit level, i.e., offered eight virtual GPUs for each physical GPU.超额订阅级别，即为每块物理 GPU 提供 8 块虚拟 GPU。

    We specify which resource name to use (e.g., nvidia.com/gpu or nvidia.com/gpu.shared) and a replicas count. By setting nvidia.com/gpu with replicas: 8, each physical GPU exposes eight schedulable units. Consequently, the node’s nvidia.com/gpu label displays the total virtual GPU count (8 for one GPU, 80 for ten). A gpu.replicas=8 label also gets added to the node to signify this oversubscription. Optionally, you can rename the shared resource to nvidia.com/gpu.shared to distinguish it from truly exclusive GPUs by setting renameByDefault to true.

    我们指定要使用的资源名（如 nvidia.com/gpu 或 nvidia.com/gpu.shared）以及 replicas 数量。把 nvidia.com/gpu 设为 replicas: 8 后，每块物理 GPU 暴露 8 个可调度单元。相应地，节点的 nvidia.com/gpu 标签显示虚拟 GPU 总数（一块 GPU 为 8，十块为 80）；节点还会被加上 gpu.replicas=8 标签来标明这种超额订阅。可选地，把 renameByDefault 设为 true，即可把共享资源重命名为 nvidia.com/gpu.shared，以区别于真正独占的 GPU。

    Unlike MIG, time slicing does not provide memory or fault isolation between the pods sharing the GPU. All pods on the same physical GPU have access to the entire GPU memory and share the same fault domain. This means if one process crashes the GPU (like an illegal memory access causing a GPU reset), it will affect the other workloads on that GPU as well. Also, if one pod grabs most of the GPU’s memory, the others may fail to allocate memory. Time slicing guarantees only a share of compute time, not memory quotas. This lack of memory isolation means you must carefully size your workloads to ensure they collectively fit within the GPU’s available memory.

    与 MIG 不同，时间切片在共享 GPU 的 pod 之间不提供显存隔离或故障隔离。同一物理 GPU 上的所有 pod 都能访问整块 GPU 显存，并共享同一个故障域。这意味着如果某个进程搞崩了 GPU（例如非法显存访问导致 GPU 复位），也会影响该 GPU 上的其他负载。此外，如果某个 pod 占走大部分 GPU 显存，其他 pod 可能分配不到显存。时间切片只保证一份计算时间份额，不保证显存配额。这种显存隔离的缺失意味着你必须仔细估算各负载的大小，确保它们合起来不超过 GPU 的可用显存。

    原书第 137 页

    Requesting multiple time-sliced GPUs

    A pod requesting multiple time-sliced GPUs (e.g., nvidia.com/gpu: 2 when GPUs are in shared mode) doesn’t give you twice the performance of a single GPU. Instead, it receives shares on two separate physical GPUs, each shared with other workloads, which is rarely useful. To prevent this confusion, the device plug-in can be configured to reject requests for more than one GPU in shared mode. Time-slicing is intended for scenarios where each pod requests exactly one GPU, understanding that this “one GPU” represents a fraction of a physical GPU. For multi-GPU workloads, keep those GPUs exclusive or use MIG.

    一个 pod 请求多块时间切片 GPU（例如在 GPU 处于共享模式时写 nvidia.com/gpu: 2）并不会给你两倍于单块 GPU 的性能。相反，它会在两块不同的物理 GPU 上各拿到一份份额，而每块 GPU 又都与其他负载共享——这很少有用。为避免这种困惑，设备插件可配置为在共享模式下拒绝请求多块 GPU。时间切片面向的场景是：每个 pod 恰好请求一块 GPU，并理解这块“一块 GPU”其实只是物理 GPU 的一部分。对于多 GPU 负载，请把那些 GPU 独占，或使用 MIG。

    Time slicing is great for oversubscribing GPUs in environments where workloads are bursty or lightweight. For example, if you have a powerful GPU but lots of small inference tasks or interactive notebooks, you could run several on one GPU so it’s utilized more efficiently. Each job might run a bit slower if they all truly contend for GPU, but overall throughput can improve. Time slicing also allows older GPUs (that don’t support MIG) to be shared. If you have NVIDIA T4 or V100 GPUs in a lab cluster running many smaller models, time slicing might let you run two or three per GPU concurrently, maximizing hardware use. Just be mindful of the lack of memory isolation: you must size your models so that together they fit in GPU RAM. Admittedly, time slicing might not be so useful in the context of LLMs, which are typically so large that they need to allocate the full physical memory offered by a GPU.

    在负载突发或轻量的环境中，时间切片非常适合做 GPU 超额订阅。例如，如果你有一块强力 GPU，但有很多小推理任务或交互式 notebook，可以在一块 GPU 上跑好几个，让它利用得更充分。如果它们真的争用 GPU，每个任务可能跑得稍慢，但整体吞吐可以提升。时间切片还让较老、不支持 MIG 的 GPU 也能被共享。如果你的实验室集群里有 NVIDIA T4 或 V100 GPU、跑着许多较小模型，时间切片或许能让你在每块 GPU 上并发跑两三个，最大化硬件利用。只需留意显存隔离的缺失：你必须估算好模型大小，使它们合起来装进 GPU 显存。平心而论，时间切片在 LLM 场景下未必那么有用——LLM 通常大到需要占满整块 GPU 的物理显存。

    For scenarios requiring stronger isolation guarantees and fixed memory allocations per workload, NVIDIA offers a hardware-based solution called Multi-Instance GPU (MIG).

    对于需要更强隔离保证、以及每负载固定显存分配的场景，NVIDIA 提供了一种基于硬件的方案，称为 Multi-Instance GPU（MIG）。

    Multi-Instance GPU

    NVIDIA Ampere and newer GPUs (like A100, A30, H100, and Blackwell B100/B200) offer MIG, a feature that lets you partition a physical GPU into several hardware-isolated instances. Each instance (or MIG slice) has its own dedicated compute cores, memory carve-out, and even separate engine contexts—it’s like having multiple smaller GPUs in one card. For example, an A100 40-GB GPU can be split into up to seven MIG instances. The smallest configuration is 1g.5gb (one GPU slice with five GB memory each). Each MIG device acts like a mini GPU with guaranteed memory and isolated Streaming Multiprocessor (SM) resources.

    NVIDIA Ampere 及更新的 GPU（如 A100、A30、H100 以及 Blackwell B100/B200）提供 MIG——这一特性让你把一块物理 GPU 分区为若干硬件隔离的实例。每个实例（或称 MIG slice）都有自己专用的计算核心、显存切分，甚至独立的引擎上下文——就像在一张卡里装了多块较小的 GPU。例如，一块 A100 40-GB GPU 最多可切成 7 个 MIG 实例；最小配置是 1g.5gb（每个 GPU slice 5 GB 显存）。每个 MIG 设备就像一块迷你 GPU，有受保障的显存与隔离的流式多处理器（SM）资源。

    原书第 138 页

    The NVIDIA device plug-in can expose MIG partitions as schedulable resources in two ways:

    NVIDIA 设备插件可以通过两种方式把 MIG 分区暴露为可调度资源：

  • Single MIG strategy. All MIG instances on a node are advertised under the generic nvidia.com/gpu resource (just like normal GPUs). This strategy assumes each GPU is identically partitioned. For instance, if every A100 on the node is split into seven 5-GB instances, a node with two A100s would report nvidia.com/gpu: 14. When a pod requests one GPU, it actually gets one MIG slice (5 GB). The node labels (gpu.product, gpu.count, etc.) are adjusted to reflect MIG (you’d see gpu.product = ...-MIG-1g.5gb and gpu.count = 14 in the example). This approach keeps things simple for users but requires homogeneous MIG setup on all GPUs.Single MIG 策略。节点上所有 MIG 实例都在通用资源 nvidia.com/gpu 下公布（就像普通 GPU 一样）。该策略假设每块 GPU 的分区方式完全相同。例如，如果节点上每块 A100 都切成 7 个 5 GB 实例，那么一块带两块 A100 的节点会上报 nvidia.com/gpu: 14。当 pod 请求一块 GPU 时，它实际拿到的是一个 MIG slice（5 GB）。节点标签（gpu.product、gpu.count 等）会被调整以反映 MIG（在该例中你会看到 gpu.product = ...-MIG-1g.5gb、gpu.count = 14）。这种方式对用户来说简单，但要求所有 GPU 的 MIG 设置同质。
  • Mixed MIG strategy. MIG instances are exposed as distinct resource types, named by their MIG profile (e.g., nvidia.com/mig-1g.5gb, nvidia.com/mig-4g.20gb, etc.). In this mode, a node with an A100 might advertise several different resources if it has a mix of MIG sizes. A user can request a specific MIG size by using the corresponding resource name in the pod spec. For example, a pod could request nvidia.com/mig-2g.10gb: 1 to get a roughly 10-GB MIG instance. This strategy is more flexible (GPUs in a node could be split differently or even remain whole), but it’s a bit more advanced to schedule since users need to know which MIG type to ask for.Mixed MIG 策略。MIG 实例作为不同的资源类型暴露，按其 MIG profile 命名（如 nvidia.com/mig-1g.5gb、nvidia.com/mig-4g.20gb 等）。在这种模式下，如果一块带 A100 的节点上 MIG 大小不一，它可能公布好几种不同资源。用户可以在 pod 规范中使用相应的资源名来请求特定 MIG 大小。例如，pod 可以请求 nvidia.com/mig-2g.10gb: 1，以获得一个约 10 GB 的 MIG 实例。这种策略更灵活（节点中的 GPU 可以切法不同，甚至保持整块），但调度上稍高级——用户需要知道该请求哪种 MIG 类型。

    • In both cases, the GPU Operator’s MIG manager will handle creating the MIG partitions on the GPU as specified by the mig.strategy in the ClusterPolicy (either single or mixed), as shown in Example 3-11. If MIG mode is off (none strategy), then GPUs are not partitioned at all.

    在两种情况下，GPU Operator 的 MIG manager 都会按 ClusterPolicy 中 mig.strategy（single 或 mixed）的指定，在 GPU 上创建 MIG 分区，如例 3-11 所示。如果 MIG 模式关闭（none 策略），则 GPU 完全不分区。

    Unlike time slicing, MIG provides strong isolation. Each MIG instance has a fixed fraction of the GPU’s memory. It cannot use more than its allocation, which prevents one workload from stealing the memory of the others. Fault isolation is also improved: if one MIG instance crashes or resets, the others can continue unaffected. This makes MIG attractive for multitenant or production scenarios where you want to safely run different applications on the same physical GPU. This is ideal if each model service needs only a few GBs of GPU memory.

    与时间切片不同，MIG 提供强隔离。每个 MIG 实例有固定比例的 GPU 显存，不能超出其分配，从而防止某个负载抢占其他负载的显存。故障隔离也更好：如果一个 MIG 实例崩溃或复位，其他实例可不受影响地继续运行。这使 MIG 在多租户或生产场景中很有吸引力——你想在同一块物理 GPU 上安全运行不同应用。如果每个模型服务只需要几 GB GPU 显存，MIG 就非常理想。

    The trade-off is granularity and overhead. You are limited to the MIG profiles defined by NVIDIA (you can’t create an arbitrary 6-GB slice, only the fixed sizes offered by the card). Also, if one job could have used the whole GPU at times, MIG partitions mean the job is hard-limited to its share—there’s no concept of borrowing unused capacity from others. In contrast, time slicing could let one pod burst to use the whole GPU if the others are idle (because nothing prevents it from grabbing more memory or compute when available, whereas MIG would keep it confined).

    权衡在于粒度与开销。你被限制在 NVIDIA 定义的 MIG profile 内（不能随意切出 6 GB 的 slice，只能用显卡提供的固定规格）。此外，如果某个任务有时本可以用满整块 GPU，MIG 分区意味着它被硬限制在自己的份额内——没有“借用他人空闲容量”的概念。相比之下，如果其他 pod 空闲，时间切片可以让一个 pod 突发用满整块 GPU（因为没有什么阻止它在有空闲时抢占更多显存或算力，而 MIG 会把它限制住）。

    原书第 139 页

    Therefore, MIG is best when you have fairly steady parallel uses for the GPU that each fit in a partition. For LLM and generative AI workloads, MIG is particularly useful for inference serving scenarios or running many smaller experiments. If you have a large model (that needs >40 GB, for instance), MIG won’t help—you need the full GPU or multiple GPUs. But if you’re hosting multiple smaller models (say, seven different language models each requiring ~5 GB), MIG can be very helpful, effectively giving each model its own virtual GPU with guaranteed memory.

    因此，当你对 GPU 有相当稳定的并行用途、且每个用途都能装进一个分区时，MIG 最合适。对 LLM 与生成式 AI 负载，MIG 在推理服务场景或运行许多较小实验时特别有用。如果你有一个大模型（例如需要 >40 GB），MIG 帮不上忙——你需要整块 GPU 或多块 GPU。但如果你在托管多个较小模型（比如 7 个不同语言模型、每个约需 5 GB），MIG 就非常有用——它实际上给每个模型一块自带受保障显存的虚拟 GPU。

    Interestingly, time slicing and MIG aren’t mutually exclusive. You can time slice MIG instances too. For example, you could split a GPU into two MIG instances, and then oversubscribe each MIG instance twice with time slicing. This would present four schedulable units per GPU. This is advanced and needed only in corner cases—but the operator does support it (appending -SHARED to MIG device product labels if both are enabled). You might do this if you want the memory isolation of MIG (say, two big slices) but also want to occasionally run two pods in one slice. However, for most, it’s either MIG or time-shared, not both simultaneously, due to complexity in managing performance.

    有趣的是，时间切片与 MIG 并不互斥。你也可以对 MIG 实例做时间切片。例如，你可以把一块 GPU 切成两个 MIG 实例，再用时间切片把每个 MIG 实例超额订阅两次，这样每块 GPU 就呈现 4 个可调度单元。这是高级玩法，只在边角场景才需要——但 operator 确实支持（若两者都启用，会在 MIG 设备 product 标签后加 -SHARED）。当你既想要 MIG 的显存隔离（比如两大块 slice）、又想偶尔在一个 slice 里跑两个 pod 时，可以这么做。但对大多数人，出于性能管理的复杂性，二者通常二选一，不同时用。

    To summarize the difference, MIG partitions a GPU into smaller dedicated slices (each with fixed memory and compute capacity), whereas time slicing treats the whole GPU as a single pool that multiple jobs take turns using, sharing time but not guaranteeing memory splits. MIG gives you isolation and predictability, while time slicing gives you flexibility and potentially higher utilization if not all jobs are busy at once. For LLM training (which often consumes entire GPUs or multiple GPUs), typically neither MIG nor time slicing is used—you just allocate GPUs exclusively. But for LLM inference and related workloads (fine-tuning smaller models, running many experiments, serving many models), both MIG and time slicing are very useful. A common pattern is to use MIG for strict multitenancy or production QA tests, and use time slicing in dev environments or for oversubscribing on less critical batch jobs where you don’t mind if they slow each other down. To verify that your GPU sharing configuration works as expected, nvidia-smi is your go-to diagnostic tool.

    总结一下二者区别：MIG 把 GPU 分区为较小的专用 slice（每个有固定显存与算力），而时间切片把整块 GPU 当作一个池，多个任务轮流使用——共享时间但不保证显存切分。MIG 给你隔离与可预测性，时间切片则给你灵活性，且在并非所有任务都同时忙碌时可能带来更高利用率。对于 LLM 训练（常占满整块或多块 GPU），通常既不用 MIG 也不用时间切片——你直接独占分配 GPU。但对于 LLM 推理及相关负载（微调较小模型、跑许多实验、服务许多模型），MIG 与时间切片都很有用。一个常见模式是：严格多租户或生产 QA 测试用 MIG；开发环境、或在不太关键的批处理作业上做超额订阅时用时间切片（那些作业互相拖慢也无所谓）。要验证 GPU 共享配置是否如预期工作，nvidia-smi 是你的首选诊断工具。

    原书第 140 页

    GPU Diagnostics with nvidia-smi

    nvidia-smi is NVIDIA’s System Management Interface tool, providing real-time monitoring and management of NVIDIA GPU devices. It offers insights into GPU utilization, memory usage, temperature, power consumption, and active processes. By executing nvidia-smi, users can obtain a snapshot of the current state of all GPUs in the system. For continuous monitoring, the -l flag can be used to refresh the output at specified intervals (e.g., nvidia-smi -l 5 updates every 5 seconds). This tool is invaluable for diagnosing performance issues, ensuring that GPUs are operating within optimal parameters, and verifying that applications are utilizing GPU resources as intended. Additionally, it aids in detecting anomalies such as thermal throttling or unexpected memory consumption, facilitating proactive troubleshooting in GPU-accelerated environments.

    nvidia-smi 是 NVIDIA 的系统管理接口工具，提供对 NVIDIA GPU 设备的实时监控与管理。它能让你洞察 GPU 利用率、显存使用、温度、功耗与活动进程。执行 nvidia-smi，用户可获得系统中所有 GPU 当前状态的快照。要持续监控，可用 -l 标志按指定间隔刷新输出（例如 nvidia-smi -l 5 每 5 秒更新一次）。该工具对诊断性能问题、确保 GPU 运行在最优参数内、以及验证应用是否按预期使用 GPU 资源都非常宝贵。此外，它还有助于检测热节流、异常显存消耗等异常，便于在 GPU 加速环境中主动排障。

    As shown in Example 3-13, you can easily run it directly with kubectl, too.

    如例 3-13 所示，你也可以很方便地直接用 kubectl 运行它。

    Example 3-13. Example of running nvidia-smi directly on a GPU-enabled Kubernetes node

    patch=$(cat <<EOT
[{
  "op":"add",
  "path":"/spec/containers/0/resources",
  "value":{"limits":{"nvidia.com/gpu":1}}
}]
EOT
)

kubectl run --rm -it gpu-pod \
  --image=nvidia/cuda:12.8.1-base-ubi9 \
  --restart=Never \
  --overrides=$patch --override-type=json -- nvidia-smi

    Sub-GPU techniques like time slicing or MIGs are useful for squeezing many small or midsized models onto the same card, but LLMs rarely fall into that category. In practice, the bottleneck is not how to split one GPU—it is that even the biggest card is still too small. This brings us to the inverse problem. Instead of sharing one GPU across many workloads, we must distribute a single workload across many GPUs. Multi-GPU inference addresses this challenge by coordinating multiple GPUs, sometimes across several nodes, to serve a single large model.

    时间切片、MIG 这类子 GPU 技术，适合把许多中小型模型挤到同一张卡上，但 LLM 很少属于这一类。实践中，瓶颈不在于如何切分一块 GPU——而在于即便最大的卡也还是太小。这就把我们带到了反向问题：不是把一块 GPU 共享给许多负载，而是必须把单个负载分布到多块 GPU 上。多 GPU 推理通过协调多块 GPU（有时跨多个节点）来服务单个大模型，从而应对这一挑战。

    原书第 141 页

    Multi-GPU Inference
    多 GPU 推理

    In the previous section we learned how to divide a single physical GPU among many workloads. For LLMs, serving the inverse situation is far more common. Running inference for LLMs often demands more GPU memory and compute than a single GPU can provide.

    上一节我们学习了如何把单块物理 GPU 分给许多负载。对 LLM 而言，反过来的情形要常见得多：运行 LLM 推理所需的显存与算力，常常超过单块 GPU 所能提供的。

    When using multiple GPUs for LLM inference, there are two fundamental approaches, each serving different needs. Figure 3-1 shows the taxonomy of multi-GPU parallelism strategies.

    用多块 GPU 做 LLM 推理时，有两种基本方式，各服务不同需求。图 3-1 展示了多 GPU 并行策略的分类。

    Data parallelism uses multiple GPUs to host replicas of the same model, serving different requests in parallel to increase overall queries per second (QPS). In contrast, model parallelism is required when a single model is too large to fit into one GPU’s memory—the model is split across GPUs so that each GPU holds part of the model and collectively they handle one inference request. Model parallelism can be further divided into tensor parallelism, which splits individual model layers across GPUs on a single node, and pipeline parallelism, which distributes entire model layers across multiple nodes.

    数据并行用多块 GPU 承载同一模型的多个副本，并行服务不同请求，以提高整体每秒查询数（QPS）。相比之下，当单个模型大到装不进一块 GPU 的显存时，就需要模型并行——模型被拆分到多块 GPU 上，每块 GPU 持有模型的一部分，共同处理一次推理请求。模型并行又可细分为：张量并行，把单层模型拆分到单节点内的多块 GPU 上；流水线并行，把整层模型分布到多个节点上。

    Let’s examine each approach in detail, starting with data parallelism.

    我们逐一细看，先从数据并行开始。

    Data Parallelism

    Data parallelism increases overall throughput by running multiple complete copies of the model. In this scenario, each GPU holds the full model and serves different requests concurrently. When a model is too large for one GPU, each group of GPUs working together via model parallelism can also run an independent replica. This approach does not accelerate any single query’s latency, but it allows more queries to be processed in parallel, thereby boosting QPS. For example, if you have four GPUs and a moderate-sized LLM that fits in one GPU, you can deploy four separate model instances with each GPU running one instance to handle four times the traffic. The Kubernetes-native approach is to run multiple replica pods, each requesting one GPU

    数据并行通过运行模型的多个完整副本来提升整体吞吐。在这种场景中，每块 GPU 持有完整模型，并并发服务不同请求。当模型大到单块 GPU 装不下时，每一组通过模型并行协同工作的 GPU 也可以运行一个独立副本。这种方式不会加快单次查询的延迟，但它让更多查询被并行处理，从而提升 QPS。例如，如果你有四块 GPU、一个中等大小、能装进一块 GPU 的 LLM，就可以部署四个独立模型实例，每块 GPU 跑一个实例，处理四倍流量。Kubernetes 原生的做法是运行多个副本 pod，每个请求一块 GPU——

    原书第 142 页

    and serving the model behind a load balancer service, which enables automatic load distribution. Alternatively, some inference frameworks use a multithreaded server within a single pod that dispatches requests to multiple GPUs, though this is less common for GPU workloads in Kubernetes.

    并在一个负载均衡 service 后面服务模型，从而实现自动负载分发。另一种做法是，某些推理框架在单个 pod 内使用多线程服务器，把请求分派到多块 GPU——不过这在 Kubernetes 的 GPU 负载中较少见。

    Figure 3-2 shows how to fan out to multiple replicas of the same model for many concurrent requests.

    图 3-2 展示了如何为大量并发请求把请求扇出到同一模型的多个副本。

    Data parallelism is ideal when you need to serve many simultaneous users or API requests and the model fits in a single GPU’s memory. For instance, an LLM with 7B parameters can often be quantized to 8 GB of memory, fitting on a 16-GB GPU—you might run 8 replicas on 8 GPUs to handle lots of chats in parallel. The limitation is that this does nothing to reduce the latency of a single query. Each query is still processed by one GPU from start to finish when the model is not parallelized, so if you have a single very large request that one GPU would take 10 seconds to handle, adding more GPUs for data parallelism won’t speed up that one request—it will just allow handling other requests concurrently. In fact, serving a single request on multiple model replicas would be wasteful because it consumes multiple GPUs to process the same input without reducing latency—instead, model parallelism, as described in “Model Parallelism” on page 106, is needed for that case.

    当你需要服务大量并发用户或 API 请求、且模型能装进单块 GPU 显存时，数据并行是理想选择。例如，一个 7B 参数的 LLM 常可量化到 8 GB 显存，装进一块 16 GB GPU——你可以在 8 块 GPU 上跑 8 个副本，并行处理大量对话。局限在于：它对降低单次查询的延迟毫无帮助。当模型未并行化时，每次查询仍由一块 GPU 从头到尾处理；所以如果你有一个超大请求、单块 GPU 要花 10 秒处理，加更多 GPU 做数据并行并不会让这一个请求变快——它只是让你能并发处理其他请求。事实上，把单个请求放到多个模型副本上服务是浪费的，因为它消耗多块 GPU 处理同一输入却不降低延迟——那种场景需要的是模型并行，如第 106 页“模型并行”所述。

    Another limitation is resource usage: running N replicas means storing N copies of the model weights in memory. This can be inefficient if the model is large and memory is limited. Some frameworks support multistream batching on a single model instance to improve utilization (e.g. vLLM, described in “vLLM” on page 8, can dynamically batch multiple incoming queries on one GPU to improve throughput), which is an alternative to full replication. In summary, data parallelism via multiple GPUs is straightforward, typically implemented as horizontal scaling of pods, but be mindful that it increases memory footprint linearly and saturates overall GPU compute only if you indeed have enough concurrent load. If request rate is low,

    另一个局限是资源使用：跑 N 个副本意味着在内存中存 N 份模型权重。如果模型大、显存有限，这可能低效。有些框架在单个模型实例上支持多流批处理以提高利用率（例如 vLLM，见第 8 页“vLLM”，它能在一块 GPU 上动态批处理多个进来的查询以提升吞吐），这是完全复制之外的另一种选择。总之，用多 GPU 做数据并行很直接，通常实现为 pod 的水平扩缩；但要注意它线性增加显存占用，且只有在你确实有足够并发负载时才会饱和整体 GPU 算力。如果请求率低，

    原书第 143 页

    those extra GPUs might sit idle—in which case, one might consolidate work onto fewer GPUs or even share GPUs among multiple models via time slicing or MIG, as described in “Sub-GPU Allocation” on page 98. For dynamic workloads, you can also leverage Kubernetes autoscaling to automatically adjust the number of replicas based on demand (see the Elastic Scale pattern in Kubernetes Patterns).

    那些额外的 GPU 可能闲置——这时或许该把工作合并到更少的 GPU 上，甚至通过时间切片或 MIG 让多个模型共享 GPU（见第 98 页“子 GPU 分配”）。对于动态负载，你还可以利用 Kubernetes 自动扩缩容，按需求自动调整副本数（见《Kubernetes Patterns》中的 Elastic Scale 模式）。

    Model Parallelism
    模型并行

    The second motive for multi-GPU inference is to allow a single large model to be served by multiple GPUs in unison. Unlike data parallelism, which replicates the entire model, model parallelism splits a single model across multiple GPUs—necessary for modern LLMs with tens or hundreds of billions of parameters that exceed the memory of one GPU. This is possible because LLMs have a layered architecture composed of sequential transformer layers. This structure allows splitting the model in two ways: tensor parallelism divides the computations within each layer across GPUs, while pipeline parallelism assigns different layers to different GPUs. Both approaches can be combined for very large deployments, and in each case, individual GPUs hold a portion of the neural network and compute part of the forward pass. Model parallelism focuses on reducing per-GPU memory usage and potentially latency for one inference by leveraging multiple devices in parallel, at the cost of added communication between GPUs. High-bandwidth interconnects (like NVIDIA NVLink or NVSwitch, explained in the following sidebar) are often critical here to handle the frequent data exchanges without bottlenecks.

    多 GPU 推理的第二个动机，是让单块大模型由多块 GPU 协同服务。数据并行复制整个模型，而模型并行把单个模型拆分到多块 GPU 上——这对于参数量达数百亿、超出单块 GPU 显存的现代 LLM 是必需的。之所以可行，是因为 LLM 具有由顺序 transformer 层组成的分层架构。这种结构允许以两种方式切分模型：张量并行把每一层内部的计算分到多块 GPU 上；流水线并行则把不同层分配到不同 GPU。两种方式在超大规模部署中可以组合；在每种情况下，各 GPU 持有神经网络的一部分，计算前向传播的一部分。模型并行通过并行利用多块设备来降低单 GPU 显存占用、并可能降低单次推理延迟，代价是 GPU 间通信增加。高带宽互连（如 NVIDIA NVLink 或 NVSwitch，见下面侧栏）在这里往往很关键，可避免频繁数据交换成为瓶颈。

    NVLink and NVSwitch: NVIDIA GPU Interconnects

    NVIDIA developed two complementary technologies to enable high-speed GPU-to-GPU communication for model parallelism: NVLink for direct connections and NVSwitch for fabric-based networking.

    NVIDIA 开发了两种互补技术，为模型并行提供高速 GPU 间通信：NVLink 用于直连，NVSwitch 用于基于交换网的网络。

    NVLink is a high-speed, point-to-point interconnect that provides direct GPU-to-GPU communication within a server node. The fifth-generation, NVLink 5.0 (introduced with the Blackwell architecture), delivers up to 1.8 TBps bidirectional bandwidth per GPU using 18 links at 100 GBps each. This represents a 2× improvement over the previous NVLink 4.0 generation (900 GBps on H100 GPUs), and over 14× the bandwidth of PCIe Gen5. Early NVLink generations supported connecting 4 to 8 GPUs; modern implementations can scale to 576 GPUs, though practical deployments typically use 8 GPUs per node.

    NVLink 是一种高速点对点互连，在服务器节点内提供直接的 GPU 间通信。第五代 NVLink 5.0（随 Blackwell 架构推出）通过 18 条各 100 GBps 的链路，为每块 GPU 提供高达 1.8 TBps 的双向带宽。这比上一代 NVLink 4.0（H100 GPU 上 900 GBps）提升 2 倍，是 PCIe Gen5 带宽的 14 倍以上。早期 NVLink 代际支持连接 4 到 8 块 GPU；现代实现可扩展到 576 块 GPU，但实际部署通常每节点用 8 块 GPU。

    NVSwitch is a high-performance switching fabric (a switching network architecture) that extends NVLink connectivity into a fully connected, nonblocking mesh where any GPU can communicate with any other GPU at full NVLink bandwidth simultaneously. NVSwitch 4.0 (for Blackwell systems) features 72 NVLink 5.0 ports per chip; a dual-chip switch tray provides 144 ports and 14.4 TBps switching capacity. NVIDIA HGX H100 and H200 systems use 4 NVSwitch 3.0 chips to interconnect 8 GPUs, while the GB200 NVL72 rack-scale system connects 72 GPUs across multiple servers using NVLink Switch with 144 ports and 130 TBps of total GPU bandwidth. The key distinction: NVLink provides the physical interconnect links, while NVSwitch provides the switching infrastructure to scale these connections across many GPUs. For cross-node communication in multiserver clusters, systems combine NVLink/NVSwitch for intra-node communication with InfiniBand or RoCE networks for inter-node traffic. GPUDirect RDMA technology bridges these layers, enabling direct GPU-to-GPU data transfers across network boundaries without CPU involvement.

    NVSwitch 是一种高性能交换网（一种交换网络架构），把 NVLink 连接扩展为全连接、无阻塞的 mesh，任意 GPU 都能同时以完整 NVLink 带宽与其他 GPU 通信。NVSwitch 4.0（面向 Blackwell 系统）每颗芯片有 72 个 NVLink 5.0 端口；双芯片交换托盘提供 144 个端口与 14.4 TBps 的交换容量。NVIDIA HGX H100 与 H200 系统用 4 颗 NVSwitch 3.0 芯片互连 8 块 GPU；GB200 NVL72 机架级系统则用带 144 端口、总算力带宽 130 TBps 的 NVLink Switch，跨多台服务器连接 72 块 GPU。关键区别是：NVLink 提供物理互连链路，NVSwitch 提供把这些连接扩展到多块 GPU 的交换基础设施。对于多服务器集群中的跨节点通信，系统把 NVLink/NVSwitch（用于节点内通信）与 InfiniBand 或 RoCE 网络（用于节点间流量）结合。GPUDirect RDMA 技术桥接这些层，实现跨网络边界的直接 GPU 间数据传输，而无需 CPU 参与。

    These technologies come with significant cost considerations. Deployments involving NVSwitch-based systems can reach multimillion-dollar price points and require substantial power and cooling infrastructure. However, for training LLMs and running inference on models exceeding single-GPU memory capacity, the bandwidth and low-latency characteristics of NVLink and NVSwitch are often essential to achieve acceptable performance.

    这些技术伴随高昂的成本考量。采用 NVSwitch 系统的部署可达数百万美元的价格，并需要庞大的供电与散热基础设施。然而，对于训练 LLM、以及对超出单 GPU 显存的模型做推理，NVLink 与 NVSwitch 的高带宽、低延迟特性往往是达到可接受性能所必需的。

    原书第 144 页

    Tensor parallelism

    Tensor parallelism slices the computations within each layer across multiple GPUs, as illustrated in Figure 3-3. In this scheme, each GPU holds a shard of the layer’s weights (for example, splitting a large weight matrix by columns or rows) and processes a portion of the layer’s input. GPUs then exchange partial results to construct the full output of the layer. For instance, if a fully connected layer has a weight matrix that is too large for one GPU, it can be divided into multiple slices. Each GPU performs matrix multiplication of the input by its weight slice. The partial outputs are concatenated or summed to form the complete output. This approach keeps all GPUs busy on the same layer (improving per-token latency) and effectively multiplies the available memory bandwidth by using several GPUs in parallel.

    张量并行把每一层内部的计算切分到多块 GPU 上，如图 3-3 所示。在这种方案中，每块 GPU 持有该层权重的一个分片（例如按列或按行切分一个大权重矩阵），并处理该层输入的一部分；然后各 GPU 交换部分结果，拼出该层的完整输出。例如，如果一个全连接层的权重矩阵大到单块 GPU 放不下，就可以分成多个 slice。每块 GPU 用其权重片对输入做矩阵乘法，部分输出再拼接或求和形成完整输出。这种方式让所有 GPU 在同一层上都忙起来（改善每 token 延迟），并通过并行使用多块 GPU 有效倍增可用显存带宽。

    Tensor parallelism directly reduces the memory burden per GPU, allowing extremely large models to load. For example, splitting a 70B-parameter model across 2 to 4 GPUs means that each holds only 35B to 17.5B params.

    张量并行直接降低每块 GPU 的显存负担，让超大模型能够加载。例如，把一个 70B 参数模型分到 2 到 4 块 GPU 上，每块只持有 35B 到 17.5B 参数。

    原书第 145 页

    It also produces lower latency per token since GPUs compute in parallel. These advantages make tensor parallelism attractive for large models, but it requires significant overhead. Tensor parallelism adds frequent communication overhead—GPUs must sync after processing each layer or attention head. If the interconnect is not fast enough, communication can dominate runtime (in poorly partitioned cases, communication can consume 50 to 70% of inference time).

    由于各 GPU 并行计算，它还能降低每 token 的延迟。这些优势让张量并行对大模型很有吸引力，但它需要可观的开销。张量并行增加了频繁的通信开销——每处理完一层或一个注意力头，各 GPU 都必须同步。如果互连不够快，通信可能主导运行时间（在切分不佳的情况下，通信可能占推理时间的 50% 到 70%）。

    For this reason, tensor parallelism is best confined to single-node setups with high-bandwidth links (PCIe with NVLink or NVSwitch, as described in “NVLink and NVSwitch: NVIDIA GPU Interconnects” on page 106). In fact, fine-grained tensor parallelism across multiple nodes with standard networking is not advisable due to latency costs. We talk in more detail about single-node versus multinode setup for GPU usage later in “Single-Node Versus Multinode Inference” on page 110. In practice, the maximum tensor parallel degree is often the number of GPUs in one server (e.g., four-way tensor parallelism on a four-GPU node). Beyond that, one should either use a machine with more GPUs or switch to pipeline parallelism between nodes, which we explore next.

    因此，张量并行最好局限在带高带宽链路的单节点部署中（带 NVLink 或 NVSwitch 的 PCIe，见第 106 页“NVLink 与 NVSwitch：NVIDIA GPU 互连”）。事实上，在标准网络上跨多节点做细粒度张量并行并不可取，因为延迟代价太高。我们稍后在第 110 页“单节点 vs 多节点推理”中更详细讨论 GPU 使用的单节点与多节点部署。实践中，最大张量并行度通常就是一台服务器里的 GPU 数（例如在 4-GPU 节点上做 4 路张量并行）。超过这个数，就该要么用 GPU 更多的机器，要么在节点间改用流水线并行——接下来我们就讨论它。

    Pipeline parallelism

    Pipeline parallelism splits the model vertically by layers, assigning different consecutive layers to different GPUs, as illustrated in Figure 3-4. In this approach, the first few layers on GPU 0 process the input sequence. They then pass the intermediate activations to GPU 1 for the subsequent layers. This process continues through all pipeline stages, resembling an assembly line. Pipeline parallelism thus requires storing and transferring the intermediate activations at pipeline stages, but not every layer’s outputs as in tensor parallelism—communications happen only once per pipeline stage (per forward pass) rather than at every layer operation.

    流水线并行按层纵向切分模型，把不同的连续层分配给不同 GPU，如图 3-4 所示。在这种方式中，GPU 0 上的前几层处理输入序列，然后把中间激活值传给 GPU 1 处理后续层。这个过程贯穿所有流水线阶段，像一条装配线。因此，流水线并行需要在各阶段存储并传递中间激活值，但不像张量并行那样传递每一层的输出——通信在每个流水线阶段（每次前向传播）只发生一次，而不是每次层运算都发生。

    The key advantage of pipeline parallelism is that it minimizes inter-GPU communication frequency. Each pipeline stage requires only one activation handoff per forward pass, making pipeline parallelism more tolerant of slower interconnects. As noted earlier, this is ideal when GPUs span different servers or when high-speed interconnects like NVLink aren’t available. It allows scaling to models that exceed even a multi-GPU node’s total memory (e.g., sharding a 175B model across two nodes). However, pipeline parallelism does not improve single-request latency—in

    流水线并行的关键优势是把 GPU 间通信频率降到最低。每个流水线阶段每次前向传播只需传递一次激活值，使流水线并行对较慢互连更宽容。如前所述，当 GPU 分布在不同服务器上、或没有 NVLink 这类高速互连时，这非常理想。它让你能扩展到即便多 GPU 节点总显存也装不下的模型（例如把一个 175B 模型分片到两个节点上）。然而，流水线并行并不会改善单次请求的延迟——

    原书第 146 页

    fact, it can increase latency due to its sequential stage processing. A pipeline also introduces idle time because the next GPU in the pipeline cannot start processing the next token’s data until the previous GPU has finished the previous token, etc. Thus, unless carefully managed, multiple GPUs in a naive pipeline might be underutilized. To mitigate this, frameworks use microbatching or scheduling techniques: splitting the incoming batch or sequence into microbatches that are fed in a staggered fashion so all pipeline stages stay busy in parallel. For example, NVIDIA’s FasterTransformer and vLLM implement pipelining with automated microbatch scheduling to avoid idle times. The bottom line is that pipeline parallelism shines for multinode scaling and high-throughput batch processing (where latency of individual queries is less critical).

    事实上，由于其顺序阶段处理，它可能反而增加延迟。流水线还引入空闲时间：流水线中的下一块 GPU 必须等上一块 GPU 处理完上一个 token 后，才能开始处理下一个 token 的数据，依此类推。因此，除非精心管理，朴素流水线中的多块 GPU 可能利用不足。为缓解这一点，框架采用 microbatching 或调度技术：把进来的 batch 或序列切成 microbatch，以交错方式喂入，让所有流水线阶段并行保持忙碌。例如，NVIDIA 的 FasterTransformer 与 vLLM 实现了带自动 microbatch 调度的流水线，以避免空闲时间。总之，流水线并行在多节点扩展与高吞吐批处理（单次查询延迟不那么关键）中表现出色。

    Hybrid parallelism

    While tensor parallelism and pipeline parallelism each address different challenges, they can be combined for maximum scalability in production deployments. Many systems adopt a hybrid parallelism approach: using tensor parallelism within each node and pipeline parallelism across nodes. This hybrid approach leverages fast local links for intra-node splitting, and uses pipeline stages to span multiple machines without requiring excessive cross-node communication. The rule of thumb is: use pipeline parallelism across nodes and tensor parallelism within a node when network links are slow, but if you have a very fast interconnect between nodes, tensor parallelism can extend across nodes as well.

    张量并行与流水线并行各自应对不同挑战，但在生产部署中可以组合起来以获得最大可扩展性。许多系统采用混合并行方式：节点内用张量并行、跨节点用流水线并行。这种混合方式利用快速本地链路做节点内切分，用流水线阶段横跨多台机器，而不需要过多跨节点通信。经验法则是：当网络链路慢时，跨节点用流水线并行、节点内用张量并行；但如果你在节点间有非常快的互连，张量并行也可以跨节点延伸。

    In all cases, distributed inference requires coordination—GPUs must communicate intermediate results using collective operations (all-reduce, all-gather, send/receive, etc.), typically using NVIDIA’s NCCL library (see “What Is NCCL and RDMA?” on page 112) over high-speed links. This coordination overhead means there is some efficiency loss versus single-GPU operation, but it enables serving models of unprecedented size. It’s also worth noting that if one GPU and the node in a model-parallel group fails, the inference will fail; there is no graceful fault tolerance for a partially missing model shard. Thus, deploying model parallel inference in Kubernetes may benefit from pod affinity/anti-affinity rules (to colocate GPUs or separate failure domains) and appropriate health checks to restart the whole group if one part dies, as explained in the sidebar.

    无论哪种情况，分布式推理都需要协调——各 GPU 必须用集合通信操作（all-reduce、all-gather、send/receive 等）交换中间结果，通常经高速链路使用 NVIDIA 的 NCCL 库（见第 112 页“什么是 NCCL 与 RDMA？”）。这种协调开销意味着相比单 GPU 运行会有一些效率损失，但它让服务前所未有的大模型成为可能。还值得注意的是：如果模型并行组中某块 GPU 及其节点故障，整个推理就会失败；对部分缺失的模型分片，没有优雅的容错。因此，在 Kubernetes 中部署模型并行推理，可以受益于 pod 亲和性/反亲和性规则（把 GPU 放到一起或隔离故障域）以及适当的健康检查——当某一部分挂掉时重启整个组，如下侧栏所述。

    Controlling Pod Placement for Multi-GPU Workloads

    Kubernetes affinity and anti-affinity rules let you control where pods land relative to each other, which is essential for multi-GPU deployments.

    Kubernetes 亲和性与反亲和性规则让你能控制 pod 彼此之间的落点，这对多 GPU 部署至关重要。

    Affinity colocates pods on the same node, rack, or zone. Use this for model-parallel inference where GPUs must communicate frequently. Keeping tensor-parallel pods together on the same node minimizes latency over fast local interconnects like NVLink.

    亲和性把 pod 放到同一节点、机架或可用区。在 GPU 必须频繁通信的模型并行推理中使用它。把张量并行的 pod 放在同一节点上，可在 NVLink 等快速本地互连上把延迟降到最低。

    Anti-affinity spreads pods apart across nodes or zones. Use this for throughput-scaling deployments where independent model replicas should avoid single points of failure. If one node goes down, replicas on other nodes continue serving.

    反亲和性把 pod 分散到不同节点或可用区。在吞吐扩展部署中使用它——独立的模型副本应避免单点故障。如果一个节点宕机，其他节点上的副本继续服务。

    Both mechanisms support hard constraints (a pod will not schedule unless the rule is satisfied) and soft constraints (scheduler prefers but does not require the placement). Hard rules are critical for correctness, such as ensuring model shards land together. Soft rules optimize performance when possible but allow fallback placement. For detailed configuration and examples, see the Automated Placement pattern in Kubernetes Patterns.

    两种机制都支持硬约束（规则不满足就不调度 pod）与软约束（调度器偏好但不强制）。硬规则对正确性至关重要，例如确保模型分片落到一起；软规则在可能时优化性能，但允许回退放置。详细配置与示例见《Kubernetes Patterns》中的 Automated Placement 模式。

    原书第 147 页

    In practice, many teams keep model-parallel deployments to a single node, when possible, for simpler failure handling, and use multinode only for truly massive models. This preference raises an important question: while we’ve covered how to distribute models across GPUs using tensor and pipeline parallelism, we haven’t fully examined where those GPUs should reside from a Kubernetes deployment perspective. Should you colocate all GPUs on a single physical node, or distribute them across multiple nodes? This topology decision, independent of which parallelism strategy you choose, has profound implications for performance, reliability, and operational complexity. The following sections explore this deployment choice in detail, revisiting some familiar GPU concepts but now through the lens of node topology and Kubernetes resource constraints.

    实践中，许多团队会尽量把模型并行部署限制在单节点内，以便更简单地处理故障，只在真正超大的模型上才用多节点。这种偏好引出一个重要问题：我们已经讲了如何用张量并行与流水线并行把模型分布到多块 GPU 上，但还没有从 Kubernetes 部署视角完整考察这些 GPU 应该住在哪里。你应该把所有 GPU 集中在一个物理节点上，还是分布到多个节点？这个拓扑决策与你选择哪种并行策略无关，却对性能、可靠性与运维复杂性有深远影响。下面几节详细探讨这个部署选择，重温一些熟悉的 GPU 概念，但这次从节点拓扑与 Kubernetes 资源约束的视角来审视。

    Single-Node Versus Multinode Inference
    单节点 vs 多节点推理

    When deploying model-parallel inference on Kubernetes, you face a fundamental topology choice: concentrate your GPUs on a single node or spread them across multiple nodes. Each approach offers distinct trade-offs.

    在 Kubernetes 上部署模型并行推理时，你面临一个根本的拓扑选择：把 GPU 集中在单个节点，还是分散到多个节点。两种方式各有不同的权衡。

    Single-node multi-GPU inference means all GPUs used for the model or replicas are in the same server. As already mentioned, this has an advantage of high-speed local interconnects. Within one machine, GPUs often communicate via PCIe (and if it’s a high-end GPU-enabled server, via NVLink or NVSwitch between GPUs). For instance, NVIDIA DGX-class nodes have NVSwitch connecting all eight GPUs with up to 900 GBps bandwidth, which makes intra-node communication far faster than typical network links. As a result, parallel strategies that involve frequent communication (like tensor parallelism) work very well within a single node. In Kubernetes, utilizing multiple GPUs on one node is straightforward: you request the number of nvidia.com/gpu resources in the pod spec, and the scheduler will place the pod on a node that has that many free GPUs. The container can see all GPUs assigned to a pod (e.g., via the environment variable CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES). Your inference server or code can then initialize model parallelism across those devices.

    单节点多 GPU 推理指用于模型或副本的所有 GPU 都在同一台服务器内。如前所述，它的优势是高速本地互连。在一台机器内，GPU 通常通过 PCIe 通信（如果是高端 GPU 服务器，则通过 GPU 间的 NVLink 或 NVSwitch）。例如，NVIDIA DGX 级节点用 NVSwitch 连接全部 8 块 GPU，带宽高达 900 GBps，使节点内通信远快于典型网络链路。因此，涉及频繁通信的并行策略（如张量并行）在单节点内表现很好。在 Kubernetes 中，在一个节点上用多块 GPU 很直接：你在 pod 规范中请求 nvidia.com/gpu 资源数量，调度器就把 pod 放到一个有那么多空闲 GPU 的节点上。容器可以看到分配给该 pod 的所有 GPU（例如通过环境变量 CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES）。你的推理服务器或代码随后可以在这些设备上初始化模型并行。

    原书第 148 页

    Figure 3-5 shows how multiple GPUs can be quickly accessed on a single node.

    图 3-5 展示了在单个节点上如何快速访问多块 GPU。

    While single-node multi-GPU setups offer simplicity and high-speed interconnects, they are limited by the GPU capacity of individual servers. By contrast, multinode multi-GPU inference involves splitting the model or the serving load across GPUs that reside on different machines. This is necessary when the model is so large that no single node has enough GPU memory (for example, some teams have run 175B+ parameter models across two or more nodes with eight A100 80-GB GPUs each). In this case, the communication will go over the network interface between nodes like InfiniBand or Ethernet. As discussed in tensor parallelism (“Multi-GPU Inference” on page 104), network bandwidth between nodes (e.g., 100-Gbit Ethernet at 12.5 GBps) is an order of magnitude slower than intra-node NVLink (up to 900 GBps). This makes pipeline parallelism the preferred strategy across nodes, as it sends larger chunks less frequently.

    虽然单节点多 GPU 部署简单且有高速互连，但受限于单台服务器的 GPU 容量。相比之下，多节点多 GPU 推理把模型或服务负载拆分到位于不同机器上的 GPU 上。当模型大到没有任何单节点有足够 GPU 显存时，就必须如此（例如，有些团队在两个或更多节点上运行 175B+ 参数模型，每个节点 8 块 A100 80-GB GPU）。这种情况下，通信要走节点间的网络接口，如 InfiniBand 或以太网。如张量并行一节（第 104 页“多 GPU 推理”）所讨论，节点间网络带宽（例如 100-Gbit 以太网 12.5 GBps）比节点内 NVLink（高达 900 GBps）慢一个数量级。这使得流水线并行成为跨节点的首选策略，因为它不那么频繁地发送较大数据块。

    With pipeline parallelism, each node processes a substantial portion of the workload before passing it to the next, making the system more resilient to network latency. Additionally, if multinode is used, it’s recommended to use the fastest network available and to ensure the NCCL (NVIDIA Collective Communication Library) is configured to use RDMA (Remote Direct Memory Access) if possible. NCCL can operate over sockets or InfiniBand; in Kubernetes, you must also ensure the pods can discover each other’s addresses for NCCL (sometimes using Kubernetes service IPs or host networking for performance).

    用流水线并行时，每个节点先处理负载的相当一部分再传给下一个，使系统对网络延迟更有韧性。此外，如果用多节点，建议使用最快的可用网络，并确保 NCCL（NVIDIA 集合通信库）在可能时配置为使用 RDMA（远程直接内存访问）。NCCL 可以跑在 socket 或 InfiniBand 上；在 Kubernetes 中，你还必须确保各 pod 能为 NCCL 互相发现对方地址（有时为性能使用 Kubernetes service IP 或主机网络）。

    原书第 149 页

    What Is NCCL and RDMA?

    NCCL is a high-performance library designed for efficient GPU-to-GPU communication in multi-GPU and multinode environments. It provides optimized collective communication primitives such as all-reduce, broadcast, reduce-scatter, and all-gather, which are essential for synchronizing model parameters or intermediate results during tensor and pipeline parallelism. NCCL is typically not used directly by end users; instead, it is leveraged under the hood by inference runtimes like vLLM, and frameworks such as PyTorch, which abstract its complexity behind higher-level APIs. However, in distributed Kubernetes deployments, advanced users may need to tune NCCL-related settings (e.g., NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME) to ensure optimal performance over specific network interfaces. When available, RDMA can be used by NCCL to bypass the CPU and directly access GPU memory on remote nodes, significantly reducing latency and improving bandwidth in multinode inference setups. RDMA typically requires specialized accelerated networking devices, such as InfiniBand or RoCE-capable network adapters. Properly configured, NCCL with RDMA plays a crucial role in achieving scalable, high-throughput inference for LLMs across multiple GPUs and nodes.

    NCCL 是一个高性能库，专为多 GPU 与多节点环境中高效的 GPU 间通信而设计。它提供优化的集合通信原语，如 all-reduce、broadcast、reduce-scatter、all-gather，这些在张量并行与流水线并行中同步模型参数或中间结果时必不可少。NCCL 通常不被最终用户直接使用；相反，它在底层被 vLLM 等推理运行时以及 PyTorch 等框架所利用，后者把其复杂性抽象在更高层 API 之后。不过，在分布式 Kubernetes 部署中，高级用户可能需要调优 NCCL 相关设置（例如 NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME），以确保在特定网络接口上获得最佳性能。在可用时，NCCL 可以使用 RDMA 绕过 CPU、直接访问远端节点上的 GPU 显存，从而显著降低多节点推理部署中的延迟、提升带宽。RDMA 通常需要专用的加速网络设备，如 InfiniBand 或支持 RoCE 的网卡。配置得当时，NCCL 加 RDMA 在跨多 GPU、多节点实现可扩展、高吞吐的 LLM 推理中起关键作用。

    For multinode inference, the typical approach is to run one pod per node and coordinate them externally. Popular inference runtimes often leverage orchestration frameworks to simplify this process. For instance, in multinode deployments vLLM uses Ray, a distributed computing framework with its own scheduler, to orchestrate inference across multiple nodes. On Kubernetes, Ray runs inside pods managed by the KubeRay operator. Kubernetes still schedules and restarts pods, while Ray’s runtime coordinates distributed vLLM workers across nodes, handling task placement, node discovery, and some fault-tolerance concerns. Other runtimes, such as Hugging Face’s TGI, rely on Kubernetes-native constructs like StatefulSets or deployments, where one pod acts as a coordinator (commonly referred to as “rank-0”) and manages communication between model partitions on different pods.

    对于多节点推理，典型做法是每个节点跑一个 pod，并在外部协调它们。流行的推理运行时常借助编排框架来简化这一过程。例如，在多节点部署中，vLLM 使用 Ray——一个自带调度器的分布式计算框架——来跨多个节点编排推理。在 Kubernetes 上，Ray 运行在由 KubeRay operator 管理的 pod 内。Kubernetes 仍负责调度与重启 pod，而 Ray 的运行时跨节点协调分布式 vLLM worker，处理任务放置、节点发现以及部分容错问题。其他运行时（如 Hugging Face 的 TGI）则依赖 StatefulSet 或 deployment 等 Kubernetes 原生构造，其中一个 pod 充当协调者（通常称为 “rank-0”），管理不同 pod 上模型分区之间的通信。

    Figure 3-6 illustrates this multinode architecture, showing multiple nodes, each hosting multiple GPUs orchestrated by vLLM for inference.

    图 3-6 展示了这种多节点架构：多个节点，每个节点承载多块 GPU，由 vLLM 编排做推理。

    原书第 150 页

    Regardless of the orchestration method chosen, managing pod affinity (ensuring pods land on distinct GPU nodes or optimized locations) and service discovery (letting pods resolve each other by name or IP addresses) is essential. Kubernetes provides built-in mechanisms, such as pod hostnames and subdomains, to facilitate pod discovery. Additionally, NCCL, used by inference runtimes for efficient GPU communication, can perform topology discovery automatically within a node but typically requires explicit network interface configuration across nodes.

    无论选哪种编排方式，管理 pod 亲和性（确保 pod 落在不同 GPU 节点或优化位置）与服务发现（让 pod 按名字或 IP 互相解析）都至关重要。Kubernetes 提供内建机制（如 pod 主机名与子域名）来便利 pod 发现。此外，推理运行时用于高效 GPU 通信的 NCCL 可以在节点内自动做拓扑发现，但跨节点通常需要显式的网络接口配置。

    Latency and bandwidth differences mean that the scaling efficiency (throughput or speedup) going from single-node to multinode may drop. Within one node, you typically see near-linear speedup (e.g., four GPUs deliver approximately three and a half times the throughput of one GPU for a well-optimized model), but going multinode might give diminishing returns if the network becomes a bottleneck. Also, collective operations (like all-reduce) across nodes need to be synchronized—if one node is slightly slower or its network latency is higher, it can slow the others. This makes performance less predictable; it also means the slowest node dictates the pace (e.g., if one node’s GPU is busy with some other task or garbage collection pause, that node could stall the entire pipeline).

    延迟与带宽的差异意味着从单节点扩展到多节点时，扩展效率（吞吐或加速比）可能下降。在一个节点内，你通常看到近似线性的加速（例如，对一个优化良好的模型，4 块 GPU 约提供单块 GPU 3.5 倍的吞吐），但如果网络成为瓶颈，跨到多节点可能收益递减。此外，跨节点的集合通信操作（如 all-reduce）需要同步——如果某个节点稍慢或网络延迟更高，它会拖慢其他节点。这让性能更难预测；也意味着最慢的节点决定步调（例如，如果某节点的 GPU 在忙别的任务或因垃圾回收停顿，那个节点可能让整条流水线停滞）。

    In single-node multi-GPU inference, the failure of the node naturally leads to pod termination, which Kubernetes handles straightforwardly. In contrast, multinode model-parallel inference involves significant complexity, as a failure of any participating pod typically disrupts the entire inference job due to incomplete model partitions. Recovery usually entails restarting the full group of pods, as these distributed inference jobs require all-or-nothing semantics both for initial scheduling and recovery (a pattern known as gang scheduling, covered in detail in Chapter 7 for job scheduling). Kubernetes concepts like PodDisruptionBudgets help minimize disruptions during planned maintenance. Some advanced setups may consider checkpointing strategies to mitigate such failures, although these techniques are less common for stateless inference workloads and are more often used during training (see Chapter 6).

    在单节点多 GPU 推理中，节点故障自然导致 pod 终止，Kubernetes 直接处理即可。相比之下，多节点模型并行推理要复杂得多：任何参与 pod 的故障通常都会因模型分区不完整而中断整个推理作业。恢复通常需要重启整组 pod，因为这些分布式推理作业在初始调度与恢复时都要求全有或全无的语义（这种模式称为 gang 调度，我们将在第 7 章作业调度中详细讨论）。PodDisruptionBudget 等 Kubernetes 概念有助于在计划内维护期间尽量减少中断。一些高级部署可能考虑用 checkpoint 策略来缓解此类故障，不过这些技术在无状态推理负载中较少见，更多用于训练（见第 6 章）。

    In summary, single-node deployments remain preferable for model-parallel inference due to lower complexity and higher efficiency. However, when multinode deployments

    总之，由于复杂性更低、效率更高，模型并行推理仍优先单节点部署。但是，当多节点部署

    原书第 151 页

    are required due to model size, pipeline parallelism, expert parallelism (for Mixture-of-Experts models)2, or other network-efficient methods, combined with robust orchestration solutions like Ray.io or Kubernetes-native deployment patterns, this ensures reliable and efficient large-scale inference operations.

    因模型大小、流水线并行、专家并行（用于混合专家模型，MoE）2或其他网络高效方法而成为必需时，再结合 Ray.io 或 Kubernetes 原生部署模式等稳健编排方案，就能确保大规模推理操作可靠而高效。

    • Expert parallelism is a specialized parallelism strategy used with Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architectures, in which different “expert” subnetworks are distributed across devices. In MoE models, a routing network sends different parts of the input to different experts, so only a subset of model components is activated for each input. While powerful for certain model architectures, this technique is beyond the scope of this book.专家并行是一种专用于混合专家（MoE）架构的并行策略：不同的“专家”子网络被分布到各设备上。在 MoE 模型中，一个路由网络把输入的不同部分送往不同专家，因此每次输入只激活模型组件的一个子集。虽然对某些模型架构很强大，但该技术超出了本书范围。

    Beyond choosing the right parallelism strategy and deployment architecture, maximizing the efficiency of your GPU infrastructure requires careful attention to resource management and optimization.

    除了选择正确的并行策略与部署架构，要最大化 GPU 基础设施的效率，还需要仔细关注资源管理与优化。

    GPU Resource Optimizations
    GPU 资源优化

    This section consolidates key GPU optimization strategies for production deployments, including techniques like MIG and time slicing discussed earlier in this chapter, along with additional best practices.

    本节汇总生产部署的关键 GPU 优化策略，包括本章前面讨论过的 MIG 与时间切片等技术，以及其他最佳实践。

    Maximizing GPU utilization and avoiding unused memory is key in production LLM inference, since GPUs are expensive resources. Here are some best practices and considerations for optimizing GPU usage in a Kubernetes environment:

    在生产 LLM 推理中，最大化 GPU 利用率、避免显存闲置是关键，因为 GPU 是昂贵资源。以下是在 Kubernetes 环境中优化 GPU 使用的一些最佳实践与注意事项：

  • GPU memory defragmentation. As models load and unload, or as dynamic inference workloads allocate memory (for example, varying sequence lengths), the GPU’s memory allocator can become fragmented. This means that free memory exists in many small chunks rather than one contiguous block. This can prevent large models from being loaded, or lead to out-of-memory errors even when enough total memory is free, just not in a contiguous block. It’s often best to pre-allocate large blocks (e.g., load all model weights on startup, and use memory pools for scratch space) to avoid heap fragmentation. Frameworks like PyTorch have a caching allocator that helps, but long-running pods might still suffer fragmentation over time. If you notice GPU memory increasing or OOMs after many requests, a strategy is to periodically restart the pod to clear fragmentation. PyTorch provides an “expandable segments” feature3 that reduces fragmentation by allowing the allocator to expand existing memory segments rather than create new ones. On the inference side, vLLM’s PagedAttention is essentially a defragmentation technique for the KV cache. In order to detect memory fragmentation, a proper monitoring setup is essential. If you see that after serving many requests the available memory decreases, it’s probably because of memory defragmentation.GPU 显存碎片整理。随着模型加载与卸载，或动态推理负载分配显存（例如变化的序列长度），GPU 的显存分配器可能产生碎片。这意味着空闲显存以许多小块存在，而不是一个连续块。这会阻止大模型加载，或导致 OOM 错误——即便总有足够空闲显存，只是不在一个连续块中。通常最好预分配大块（例如启动时加载全部模型权重，并用显存池做临时空间）以避免堆碎片。PyTorch 等框架有缓存分配器帮忙，但长时间运行的 pod 仍可能随时间出现碎片。如果你注意到请求多了之后 GPU 显存增长或出现 OOM，一个策略是定期重启 pod 以清除碎片。PyTorch 提供“expandable segments”特性3，通过允许分配器扩展已有显存段而非新建段来减少碎片。在推理侧，vLLM 的 PagedAttention 本质上是一种针对 KV cache 的碎片整理技术。为检测显存碎片，适当的监控设置必不可少。如果你看到服务了很多请求后可用显存下降，很可能就是显存碎片所致。
    • See the PyTorch documentation on optimizing CUDA memory usage.参见 PyTorch 关于优化 CUDA 显存使用的文档。
    原书第 152 页
  • GPU sharing and consolidation. Aim to keep GPUs busy—an idle GPU is wasted money. If your LLM uses only 30% of a GPU’s compute and memory, consider running multiple model instances or other workloads on the same GPU. This can be done with MIG on supported hardware for clear separation (for example, two 6B-parameter models on one 80-GB A100, each in a 40-GB MIG slice) or time slicing. For more details, see “Sub-GPU Allocation” on page 98. Another approach is to run a multimodel server that loads several models onto one GPU and routes requests (if they all fit in memory). Some serving frameworks like NVIDIA Triton or AWS Multi-Model Server support multiple models per GPU, dynamically unloading less-used models if needed. The best practice is to profile your usage: if a model only uses, say, 50% of GPU memory, that remaining 50% could host another smaller model or a second copy to double throughput. Just be cautious to not overload memory—leave some margin since driver overhead and fragmentation can eat a few percent. Kubernetes doesn’t natively know if a GPU is “only half used”—it’s up to you to bin-pack wisely using MIG or by deploying multiple pods to the same node.GPU 共享与合并。目标是让 GPU 保持忙碌——空闲的 GPU 就是浪费钱。如果你的 LLM 只用了一块 GPU 30% 的算力与显存，考虑在同一块 GPU 上跑多个模型实例或其他负载。这可以在受支持的硬件上用 MIG 做清晰隔离（例如在一块 80-GB A100 上跑两个 6B 参数模型，各占一个 40-GB MIG slice），或用时间切片。更多细节见第 98 页“子 GPU 分配”。另一种做法是跑一个多模型服务器，把多个模型加载到一块 GPU 上并路由请求（前提是它们都装得下显存）。某些服务框架（如 NVIDIA Triton 或 AWS Multi-Model Server）支持每块 GPU 多模型，必要时动态卸载较不常用的模型。最佳实践是剖析你的用量：如果一个模型只用了比如 50% 的 GPU 显存，剩下 50% 可以再放一个较小模型或一份副本来把吞吐翻倍。只是要小心别让显存过载——留点余量，因为驱动开销与碎片会吃掉几个百分点。Kubernetes 天生不知道一块 GPU“只用了一半”——是否用 MIG 或在同节点部署多个 pod 来明智装箱，取决于你自己。
  • Quantization and compilation. Optimizing the model itself can reduce GPU needs. Techniques like 4-bit or 8-bit quantization of weights dramatically cut memory per model copy (at some accuracy cost). If an LLM can be quantized from 16-bit to 8-bit with negligible quality loss, you potentially halve the number of GPUs needed. Many open models have 8-bit or 4-bit quantized versions available. These allow, for instance, a 70B model to fit on a single 48-GB GPU in 4-bit mode. In full precision, this would require 280 GB (70B × 4 bytes/param), but in 4-bit mode only ~35 GB (70B × 0.5 byte/param). The vLLM and TGI servers support loading such quantized models. Additionally, consider using optimized runtimes to improve inference speed per GPU. Faster models mean you can handle more load with the same hardware, improving utilization.量化与编译。优化模型本身可以降低 GPU 需求。权重的 4-bit 或 8-bit 量化等技术能大幅降低每模型副本的显存（代价是一定精度损失）。如果一个 LLM 能从 16-bit 量化到 8-bit 而质量损失可忽略，你需要的 GPU 数可能减半。许多开源模型已有 8-bit 或 4-bit 量化版本。例如，这些让一个 70B 模型在 4-bit 模式下能装进单块 48-GB GPU。全精度需要 280 GB（70B × 4 字节/参数），而 4-bit 模式只需约 35 GB（70B × 0.5 字节/参数）。vLLM 与 TGI 服务器都支持加载此类量化模型。此外，考虑使用优化运行时来提升每块 GPU 的推理速度。模型越快，同样硬件能处理的负载越多，利用率也就越高。
  • Autoscale. Autoscaling multi-GPU deployments can be tricky if they are model-parallel. When a model is split across four GPUs, you cannot scale down to two GPUs or scale up to six GPUs. You must scale in whole replica units: either remove all four GPUs or add another complete four GPU group. But for throughput scaling, Kubernetes-based autoscaling (like with KEDA, the Horizontal Pod Autoscaler [HPA] or Knative) on RPS, concurrency or latency is effective. For comprehensive coverage of Kubernetes autoscaling patterns and best practices, see the Elastic Scale pattern in Kubernetes Patterns.自动扩缩。如果多 GPU 部署是模型并行的，自动扩缩可能比较棘手。当一个模型分到四块 GPU 上时，你不能缩到两块或扩到六块。你必须按整个副本单元扩缩：要么撤掉全部四块 GPU，要么再加一整个四 GPU 组。但对吞吐扩展，基于 Kubernetes 的自动扩缩（如 KEDA、Horizontal Pod Autoscaler [HPA] 或 Knative）按 RPS、并发或延迟来扩缩是有效的。关于 Kubernetes 自动扩缩模式与最佳实践的全面介绍，见《Kubernetes Patterns》中的 Elastic Scale 模式。
    • 原书第 153 页
  • Placement and affinity. For multi-GPU nodes it is important to know the topology. On some eight GPU servers, not all GPUs are directly connected—there might be NVLink links in a mesh or groups; e.g., a NVIDIA DGX A100 has the NVSwitch all-to-all, but other systems might have two groups of four GPUs each. If your model parallelism uses four GPUs, you might get better performance if those four are all within one NVLink group. You can use nvidia-smi topo -m to display the mesh grouping. Kubernetes won’t automatically account for that, but you can use the Node’s hardware knowledge and assign specific GPU indices by using the device plug-in capabilities to pick specific GPUs by index. Manually selecting GPU indices is an advanced optimization—for most cases, Kubernetes will just assign any four GPUs, but if you care about intra-node latency, you might pin to, say, GPU0-3 if they’re within the same NVSwitch cluster on that node.放置与亲和性。对于多 GPU 节点，了解拓扑很重要。在某些八 GPU 服务器上，并非所有 GPU 都直连——NVLink 链路可能呈 mesh 或分组；例如 NVIDIA DGX A100 是 NVSwitch all-to-all，但其他系统可能有两组各四块 GPU。如果你的模型并行用四块 GPU，把这四块都放在同一个 NVLink 组内可能获得更好性能。你可以用 nvidia-smi topo -m 显示 mesh 分组。Kubernetes 不会自动考虑这一点，但你可以利用节点的硬件知识，通过设备插件能力按索引挑选特定 GPU。手动选 GPU 索引是一种高级优化——大多数情况下 Kubernetes 随便分四块 GPU 给你；但如果你在意节点内延迟，可以钉到比如 GPU0-3（如果它们在该节点上同一个 NVSwitch 集群内）。
  • Optimize I/O and initialization. Large models take time to load from disk or network into GPU memory. If you scale pods up and down, you pay that cost each time. Amortize it by keeping pods warm, if possible. We describe optimized model loading techniques in Chapter 2.优化 I/O 与初始化。大模型从磁盘或网络加载到 GPU 显存需要时间。如果你不断扩缩 pod，每次都要付出这个代价。如果可能，让 pod 保持热态以摊销这一成本。我们在第 2 章描述了优化的模型加载技术。
  • Monitor GPU health. GPUs can encounter issues like ECC memory errors or high temperature throttling. Ensure you have node-level monitoring and alerts for such events. Kubernetes won’t automatically reschedule a pod if the GPU starts erroring but hasn’t crashed—you might need a daemon that checks with nvidia-smi for errors and then taints the node or restarts pods. Running the NVIDIA DCGM and integrating with Kubernetes node health can help. A flaky GPU in a model-parallel group can cause wrong results or crashes, so it’s important to catch hardware issues.监控 GPU 健康。GPU 可能遇到 ECC 显存错误或高温节流等问题。确保你有节点级监控与告警来应对此类事件。如果 GPU 开始报错但还没崩溃，Kubernetes 不会自动重新调度 pod——你可能需要一个 daemon 用 nvidia-smi 检查错误，然后给节点打 taint 或重启 pod。运行 NVIDIA DCGM 并与 Kubernetes 节点健康集成会有帮助。模型并行组中一块不稳定的 GPU 可能导致错误结果或崩溃，所以捕获硬件问题很重要。

    • By following these best practices—defragmenting memory, smartly sharing GPUs, leveraging scaling and optimization tools, and closely monitoring—you can achieve high utilization and reliability for multi-GPU LLM inference on Kubernetes.

    遵循这些最佳实践——整理显存碎片、明智地共享 GPU、利用扩缩与优化工具、密切监控——你就能在 Kubernetes 上实现多 GPU LLM 推理的高利用率与高可靠性。

    This completes our exploration of GPU resource optimization strategies. Having covered GPU discovery, scheduling, operator management, and multi-GPU inference strategies throughout this chapter, let’s step back and reflect on the key insights.

    这就完成了我们对 GPU 资源优化策略的探讨。本章涵盖了 GPU 发现、调度、operator 管理与多 GPU 推理策略，现在让我们退一步，回顾关键洞见。

    Lessons Learned
    经验教训

    In this chapter we explored how Kubernetes integrates GPU resources through device plug-ins, feature discovery, and advanced management capabilities for AI workloads. Kubernetes extends beyond its native CPU and memory scheduling through the device plug-in framework. Node Feature Discovery (NFD) and GPU Feature

    本章我们探讨了 Kubernetes 如何通过设备插件、特性发现以及面向 AI 负载的高级管理能力来集成 GPU 资源。Kubernetes 通过设备插件框架把原生 CPU 与内存调度扩展到 GPU。Node Feature Discovery（NFD）与 GPU Feature

    原书第 154 页

    Discovery (GFD) enable automatic detection and labeling of GPU capabilities, allowing workload-specific scheduling based on GPU model, driver version, and hardware features. This discovery layer provides the foundation for both simple resource-based scheduling and sophisticated topology-aware placement.

    Discovery（GFD）实现 GPU 能力的自动检测与打标签，从而允许基于 GPU 型号、驱动版本与硬件特性做负载专属调度。这一发现层为简单的基于资源调度与复杂的拓扑感知放置都打下了基础。

    GPU scheduling requires different strategies than traditional workloads. Resource-based scheduling allocates GPUs as countable units, while label-based scheduling with node selectors, affinity rules, and taints enables precise placement based on GPU characteristics. The emerging Dynamic Resource Allocation (DRA) API promises more flexible resource handling, although device plug-ins remain the production-ready standard for most deployments.

    GPU 调度需要与传统负载不同的策略。基于资源的调度把 GPU 作为可数单元分配；而基于标签的调度（结合节点选择器、亲和性规则与 taint）能基于 GPU 特性做精确放置。新兴的 Dynamic Resource Allocation（DRA）API 有望带来更灵活的资源处理，不过对大多数部署而言，设备插件仍是生产就绪的标准。

    Sub-GPU allocation techniques maximize hardware utilization when full GPU allocation exceeds workload requirements. Time slicing enables temporal sharing where multiple workloads alternate GPU access, suitable for inference workloads with intermittent GPU usage. Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) provides hardware-level partitioning with memory isolation, creating dedicated GPU slices with guaranteed resources and performance isolation. Each approach involves trade-offs among isolation, overhead, and scheduling complexity.

    当整块 GPU 分配超出负载需求时，子 GPU 分配技术能最大化硬件利用率。时间切片实现时间上的共享——多个负载交替访问 GPU，适合 GPU 使用时断时续的推理负载。Multi-Instance GPU（MIG）提供带显存隔离的硬件级分区，创建有资源保障与性能隔离的专用 GPU slice。每种方式都在隔离、开销与调度复杂性之间有权衡。

    Multi-GPU inference becomes necessary when models exceed single-GPU memory capacity. Tensor parallelism distributes individual operations across GPUs, requiring high-bandwidth interconnects and tight synchronization. Pipeline parallelism splits model layers across GPUs, balancing computation distribution with bubble overhead from sequential dependencies. Data parallelism replicates the entire model across GPUs, processing different batches simultaneously. These strategies demand careful orchestration across pods and nodes, with Kubernetes providing scheduling primitives, while runtime frameworks handle the coordination logic.

    当模型超出单 GPU 显存容量时，多 GPU 推理成为必需。张量并行把单次运算分布到多块 GPU 上，需要高带宽互连与紧密同步。流水线跨 GPU 切分模型层，在计算分布与顺序依赖带来的气泡开销之间取得平衡。数据并行把整个模型复制到多块 GPU 上，同时处理不同 batch。这些策略需要跨 pod 与节点的精心编排：Kubernetes 提供调度原语，运行时框架负责协调逻辑。

    The NVIDIA GPU Operator consolidates GPU management through a single operator that deploys device plug-ins, feature discovery, monitoring (DCGM), and runtime components. This declarative approach via ClusterPolicy resources simplifies GPU cluster configuration and ensures consistent GPU stack deployment across nodes, reducing operational complexity compared to manual component installation.

    NVIDIA GPU Operator 通过单个 operator 整合 GPU 管理，部署设备插件、特性发现、监控（DCGM）与运行时组件。这种通过 ClusterPolicy 资源的声明式方式简化了 GPU 集群配置，并确保跨节点一致的 GPU 栈部署，相比手动安装各组件降低了运维复杂性。

    In the next chapter, we’ll build on these GPU and infrastructure foundations to explore production readiness—covering deployment strategies, scaling patterns, performance optimization, and operational best practices for running LLM workloads reliably at scale.

    下一章，我们将在这些 GPU 与基础设施基础之上，探讨生产就绪——涵盖部署策略、扩缩模式、性能优化，以及大规模可靠运行 LLM 负载的运维最佳实践。
